title: Percutaneous coronary intervention or medical therapy alone before transcatheter aortic valve replacement: insights from a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
authors: Ahmed Elmorsy Mohamed; Mustafa Abomohsen; Muhammad Haisum Maqsood; Abdul Hakim Almakadma; Zeyad Kholeif; Ahmed Farid Gadelmawla; Rafael Harari; Susheel K Kodali; Islam Y Elgendy; Sripal Bangalore
abstract:
Coronary artery disease frequently coexists in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), yet the benefit of routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR remains uncertain.
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of routine PCI before TAVR compared with conservative or deferred revascularization.
We pooled randomized clinical trials comparing PCI before TAVR versus no/deferred PCI in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease. Random-effects models estimated pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Bayesian sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis were performed.
Three trials included 1156 patients (PCI, n = 579; no/deferred PCI, n = 577). In comparator arms reporting postrandomization PCI/revascularization, 72 of 461 patients (15.6%) underwent subsequent PCI/revascularization. PCI did not significantly reduce major adverse cardiac events (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.70-1.18; I2 = 36.9%), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.45-1.63; I2 = 49.8%), all-cause death (RR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.70-1.15; I2 = 0.0%), or stroke (RR: 0.70, 95% CI: 0.48-1.03; P = 0.069; I2 = 0.0%). In two trials, PCI reduced urgent revascularization (RR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13-0.87; I2 = 54.5%) but increased major bleeding (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32; I2 = 37.9%) and any bleeding (RR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.47; I2 = 66.7%). Bayesian analyses were directionally concordant. Trial sequential analysis was inconclusive for all efficacy outcomes.
Routine PCI before TAVR reduced urgent revascularization but increased bleeding, without significant differences in other outcomes. Current evidence remains underpowered to rule out benefit for other ischemic outcomes; larger trials are needed.

title: Covered-Stent Migration During Same-Session Aortic Isthmus Repair and Bicuspid Aortic Valve TAVR.
authors: Georgios E Papadopoulos; Ilias Ninios; Vlasis Ninios
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract: Fixed obstruction at the aortic isthmus may preclude transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Covered-stent implantation can restore large-bore access, but immediate passage of balloons and delivery systems through a newly implanted stent may expose it to longitudinal traction. Secondary stent migration during withdrawal of a valvuloplasty balloon and its intraluminal balloon-assisted rescue have not been well characterized. An 87-year-old man with New York Heart Association class III symptoms had severe bicuspid aortic stenosis (peak velocity, 4.4 m/s; mean gradient, 48 mmHg; valve area, 0.65 cm2; left ventricular ejection fraction, 55%) and a focal juxtaductal aortic-isthmus stenosis with a peak-to-peak gradient of 32 mmHg. Because of high surgical risk and unfavorable alternative access, same-session covered-stent treatment followed by transfemoral TAVR was selected. A 12 × 29-mm Advanta V12 covered stent was deployed and flared using an 18-mm noncompliant balloon. After aortic-valve predilation with a 23-mm noncompliant balloon, the stent migrated distally during balloon withdrawal. Guidewire access was preserved, and the stent remained coaxial. The balloon was recentered within the migrated stent and partially reinflated, allowing the balloon and stent to be advanced proximally as a single unit. After restoration and re-expansion of the stent, a 23-mm Myval valve was implanted successfully. Final transvalvular and isthmic gradients were 8 and 5 mmHg, respectively, with trivial paravalvular regurgitation and no aortic injury. The patient was discharged on day 3 and remained in NYHA class I at 6 months. Withdrawal of a large valvuloplasty balloon may cause secondary migration of a newly implanted aortic-isthmus stent. When guidewire access, coaxial alignment, and structural integrity are preserved, controlled intraluminal balloon-assisted repositioning may provide an effective bailout while maintaining transfemoral access.

title: Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients 50-65 Years: A Target Trial Emulation.
authors: J Hunter Mehaffey; Stanley B Wolfe; Raymond J Strobel; J W Awori Hayanga; Christopher E Mascio; Leora T Yarboro; Ramesh Daggubati; Bradley S Price; Vinay Badhwar
abstract:
Guidelines favor surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 65 years or younger with aortic stenosis, yet many receive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) without supportive data. We performed a target trial emulation of SAVR versus TAVI in this population.
Using the all-payer Premier Healthcare Database (2016-2024), patients aged 50 to 65 years undergoing isolated SAVR or TAVI within 90 days of an aortic stenosis diagnosis were evaluated. After trial exclusions, frailty and predicted risk were incorporated into a clone-censor-weight framework with inverse probability weighting. Reporting adhered to TARGET guidance. The primary outcome was the 5-year composite of all-cause mortality, stroke, valve reintervention, or heart failure rehospitalization.
The clone-censor-weighted analysis included 18,549 SAVR and 18,549 TAVI patients, balanced across all covariates (standardized mean difference <0.10). Mean age was 60 years, and many were of low surgical risk <4% (SAVR 69.5% vs TAVI 49.7%). In-hospital mortality (0.41% vs 0.31%; odds ratio, 0.61; p<0.001) and periprocedural stroke (0.31% vs 0.28%; odds ratio, 0.67; p<0.001) favored TAVI. At 5 years, risk-adjusted freedom from the primary composite outcome (87.5% vs 77.8%; hazard ratio, 1.87; p<0.001), heart failure rehospitalization (92.9% vs 88.2%; subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.72; p<0.001), and all-cause mortality (93.6% vs 85.6%; hazard ratio, 2.34; p<0.001) favored SAVR.
For contemporary patients aged 50 to 65 years, the primary composite outcome favored SAVR over TAVI at 5 years, most markedly at centers with high young TAVI utilization. These data may guide heart team decision making and future trial design.

title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.
authors: Philippe Généreux; Raj R Makkar; Philippe Pibarot; Jeroen J Bax; Brian R Lindman; Kamran Muhammad; J Bradley Oldemeyer; Mark Pirwitz; Colin M Barker; Vinod H Thourani; Pradeep K Yadav; Roberto Rodriguez; Justin Strote; Rahul Sakhuja; Ramzi Khalil; Rahul Sharma; Adnan Chhatriwalla; Jacob M Mishell; Biswajit Kar; Sameer Gafoor; Joseph Walsh; Daniel Spoon; Andrew Frutkin; Andrei Pop; Nicolas M Van Mieghem; Ruby Satpathy; Kenji Ando; Joseph Montarello; John Webb; Sreekanth Vemulapalli; David J Cohen; Aakriti Gupta; Brandon Park; Heather Prince; Philipp Blanke; Michael Mack; Martin B Leon; PROGRESS Trial Investigators
journal: The New England journal of medicine
abstract:
For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown.
We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population.
A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement.
Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

title: Advanced Cardiovascular Disease in Marbach-Rustad Progeroid Syndrome (LEMD2 p.Ser479Phe).
authors: Tacianne R B Delamain; Giseli Casarini; José H H Delamain; Cecilia Boya; Edileide B Correia; Paul Salvador; Dimytri Siqueira; Dorival Della Togna; Fausto Feres; Kleber G Franchini
abstract:
Marbach-Rustad progeroid syndrome results from the recurrent heterozygous LEMD2 c.1436C>T (p.Ser479Phe) variant. Four cases have been reported, with cardiac involvement absent or only qualitatively described.
A 30-year-old man with short stature, skeletal fragility, and facial dysmorphism presented with syncope from high-grade atrioventricular block. Echocardiography showed premature severe calcific aortic stenosis and mild mitral stenosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance showed preserved biventricular function with no late gadolinium enhancement; computed tomography confirmed valvular calcification but no coronary calcium. Chagas serology was negative. Whole-genome sequencing confirmed the p.Ser479Phe variant. He received a permanent pacemaker and, 6 months later, transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Evaluation also revealed overt type 2 diabetes, severe hypertriglyceridemia, and nephropathy: the most advanced metabolic phenotype reported.
This case shows that the p.Ser479Phe variant can cause advanced, intervention-requiring cardiovascular disease (objectively quantified and, to our knowledge, the first in vivo characterization by cardiac magnetic resonance). These findings support routine cardiac and metabolic surveillance in LEMD2-associated progeroid syndromes.

title: Recognizing Arterial Tortuosity Syndrome in Adulthood: A Case Unveiled by Stress Echocardiography.
authors: Parsa Asachi; Aditya R Gandhi; Dan Halpern; Alan F Vainrib; Muhamed Sarić
abstract:
Arterial tortuosity syndrome (ATS) is a rare autosomal recessive connective tissue disorder characterized by arterial elongation, tortuosity, and stenosis.
A 31-year-old woman with childhood peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis was referred for preconception counseling. Examination revealed a high-arched palate, narrow facies, dolichostenomelia, and joint hypermobility. Stress echocardiography demonstrated exercise-induced right ventricular systolic hypertension and incidental carotid tortuosity. Computed tomography angiography revealed tortuosity of the aortic arch, celiac trunk, and pulmonary artery branches. Genetic testing confirmed ATS. Pulmonary artery balloon angioplasty and stenting were performed. She was initiated on metoprolol and referred to maternal-fetal medicine.
ATS in adulthood may be identified following incidental findings of arterial tortuosity on imaging. ATS should be considered in patients with these findings and syndromic connective tissue features.
Imaging is crucial in diagnosing ATS. Echocardiographic findings of right ventricular systolic hypertension and arterial tortuosity should prompt consideration of ATS in the right clinical setting.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Evogliptin in Mild to Moderate Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis: The EVOID-AS Trial Rationale and Study Design.
authors: Ratnasari Padang; Roberto Hodara; M Fuad Jan; Renuka Jain; Alexander Postalian; Bryan M Zweig; Tasneem Z Naqvi; Robert A Levine; Jacob P Dal-Bianco; Edgar Argulian; Gregg S Pressman; Partho P Sengupta; Amr E Abbas; Wayne Cheng; Ankitkumar K Patel; Nicole M Bhave; Eugene S Chung; Carlos E Sanchecirf; Trace C Barrett; Smadar Kort; Jina Sohn; Peter Pollak; Mays T Ali; Scott Chadderdon; Qiong Zhao; Edward Gill; Fredy El Sakr; Naveen L Pereira; Adrian Vella; Phillip J Schulte; Kent R Bailey; Jae-Kwan Song; Jae K Oh
abstract: The only treatment of severe aortic stenosis (AS) is aortic valve replacement. No medical therapy has been proven effective for preventing or delaying AS progression despite several clinical trials. The EVOID-AS trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy of evogliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor, at retarding the progression of aortic valve calcification and AS hemodynamic severity in patients with mild to moderate AS. In this trial, 580 patients with mild or moderate native calcific AS at 40+ clinical sites across the United States and Canada will be randomized in a 1:1 allocation to receive either evogliptin 10 mg or placebo once daily orally for 2 years. Clinical follow-up visits are scheduled at 3-month intervals; transthoracic echocardiography, aortic valve computed tomography calcium score, and laboratory testing are obtained at baseline, 1-year, and 2-year study visits. The primary end point is change in aortic valve calcification as measured by cardiac computed tomography at 2 years of therapy. Secondary end points are progression of AS hemodynamic severity by echocardiography during 2 years of therapy and time to aortic valve intervention. Secondary safety end points include incidence and severity of treatment-emergent or serious adverse events. Enrollment began in June 2022, and the study is expected to be completed in 2028. EVOID-AS is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized medical trial to modify the progression of calcific AS. This trial will contribute to the critical unmet clinical need of identifying an effective medical therapy to prevent or to delay the progression of AS. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05143177.

title: Improvement in mitral regurgitation after alcohol septal ablation in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Anna Damlin; Andreas Rück; Mesud Mustafic; Rebecka Jandér; Anette Rickenlund; Maria J Eriksson; Nawzad Saleh; David Marlevi
abstract:
The primary mechanism of mitral regurgitation (MR) in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral leaflets due to septal hypertrophy narrowing the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), influencing leaflet movement and closure. Among patients undergoing alcohol septal ablation (ASA), the impact on- and underlying mechanism of MR remains less studied. The aim was to determine the prevalence of MR and changes in MR severity after ASA and analyze echocardiographic (ECHO) parameters associated with MR changes.
All patients who underwent ASA at Karolinska University Hospital in Sweden, 2009-2021 (follow-up until 2025), were included in this retrospective cohort study. ECHO parameters were collected before ASA, at 1-year follow-up and at the latest follow-up registered. To evaluate differences in continuous values, Kruskal-Wallis test was used, and for categorical values, Fischer's exact test was used.
154 patients were included (mean follow-up 4.0 ± 3.9 years). 14% (n = 21) had at least moderate MR at baseline, of which 90% (n = 19) improved to mild MR or less. The patients with improved (n = 19, 12%) or unchanged (n = 128, 83%) grade of MR showed greater reduction of LVOT peak pressure gradients (improved MR: 137.5 to 4.8 mmHg, unchanged MR: 57.0 to 25.0 mmHg) between baseline and last follow-up, compared with patients with increased MR grade (n = 7, 4.5%, 57.0 to 51.0 mmHg, p = 0.003).
Among patients with at least moderate MR before ASA, MR severity generally improved at follow-up, potentially due to septal reduction and LVOT enlargement, which may have reduced SAM.
Not applicable.

title: Cellular senescence in calcific aortic valve disease: are we ready for senolytic therapy?
authors: Ludovica Simonini; Ilenia Foffa; Augusto Esposito; Cecilia Vecoli
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is the most prevalent valvular heart disease in the Western countries and carries significant morbidity and mortality, yet no pharmacological therapy has demonstrated efficacy in modifying its natural history. Once regarded as a passive degenerative process, CAVD is now recognized as an actively regulated disease driven by endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, dysregulated mineral metabolism, and cellular senescence, which collectively drive progressive fibrotic remodeling and calcification of the valve leaflets through both dystrophic and osteogenic mechanisms. This review examines the pharmacological strategies that have been investigated or are currently under evaluation to slow CAVD progression, encompassing lipid-lowering agents, renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, bone resorption inhibitors, vitamin K supplementation, and nitric oxide pathway modulators. Despite strong biological rationale and encouraging observational or preclinical data, each of these approaches has thus far failed to demonstrate consistent disease, modifying efficacy in prospective randomized trials, reflecting the complexity of CAVD pathophysiology and the historical lack of mechanistic precision in patient selection and trial design. Emerging evidence suggests that cellular senescence may represent a unifying and potentially actionable therapeutic target, bridging endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and active calcification within a single pathophysiological framework. Preclinical studies demonstrate that senolytic clearance of senescent cells reduces calcification in atherosclerosic and hypercholesterolemic vascular models provide a compelling rationale for extending this approach to valvular targets.

title: Concomitant Transcatheter Aortic and Tricuspid Valve Replacement.
authors: Jaiel Niamat; Claire Ren; Lucas Uchoa De Assis; Antigone Kostea; Jeroen Wilschut; Rutger-Jan Nuis
abstract:
Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is associated with adverse outcomes.
A 65-year-old man with advanced right heart failure symptoms and torrential TR was accepted for transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR). After an unforeseen treatment delay, reassessment demonstrated progression of concomitant mild-to-moderate aortic stenosis (AS) to severe AS. He underwent successful TAVR and TTVR during 1 procedure with an excellent clinical outcome.
Given the sequence of disease progression with symptomatic torrential TR preceding the development of severe AS, an indication for TAVR and TTVR was established. A single-procedure strategy was favored over a staged approach based on the assumption that TAVR alone could increase forward flow and right-sided loading conditions, potentially worsening right heart failure.
Concomitant TAVR and TTVR may benefit selected patients. Pre-TAVR identification of patients requiring adjunctive TTVR and determination of the optimal timing (concomitant or staged) remain challenging.

title: Artificial Intelligence Detection of Aortic Valve Calcification on Routine Noncontrast Chest CT: A Real-World Cohort.
authors: Ofir Koren; Vivek Patel; Orit Wimpfheimer; Alexander Kukuev; Parker Chu; Harsh Jain; Kazuki Suruga; Hidemasa Shitan; Shiri Hassid; Daniel Ng; Shir Hofstetter; Raj R Makkar
abstract:
Routine noncontrast chest computed tomography (CT) may reveal aortic valve calcification (AVC) outside aortic stenosis evaluation. Its prevalence, burden, and documentation remain uncertain. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enable systematic detection.
The study aims to evaluate AVC prevalence and burden, clinical correlates, radiology documentation, and AI-assisted case finding.
This retrospective single-center study screened 511 consecutive noncontrast, non-electrocardiographically gated chest CT examinations in adults aged ≥50 years. After 15 protocol exclusions and 56 software-designated nonevaluable examinations, 440 underwent quantification by 2 blinded readers. AVC was defined as >10 AU using a 130-Hounsfield-unit threshold adjusted for blood-pool attenuation and image noise when needed. Locked HealthAVC V1.0 was a secondary comparator.
Manual quantification identified AVC in 172 of 440 scans (39.1%; 95% CI: 34.6%-43.7%); 97 of 440 (22.0%) had ≥100 AU. Inter-reader agreement at >10 AU was 99.5% (kappa = 0.990). Age (adjusted OR: 1.92 per 5 years; 95% CI: 1.63-2.26) and male sex (adjusted OR: 2.09; 95% CI: 1.32-3.30) were associated with AVC. Reports documented 27 of 172 positive scans (15.7%; 95% CI: 11.0%-21.9%). AI detected 169 of 172 manually confirmed cases (98.3%) among 440 evaluable scans, including 142 of 145 undocumented cases. Of 496 submitted scans, 56 (11.3%) were nonevaluable. End-to-end sensitivity counting positive rejected scans as missed was 89.9%. Among 86 AI-positive patients with echocardiography, 10 (11.6%) had mild-or-greater aortic stenosis.
AVC was common but infrequently documented on routine chest CT. AI detected most cases among evaluable scans; 11.3% were nonevaluable, yielding 89.9% end-to-end sensitivity. Prospective studies should assess clinical pathways.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
authors: Xiao-Fei Gao; Yan Wang; Hong Jiang; Bo Li; Yi-Bing Shao; Jun Luo; Fa-Xin Ren; Fan Ouyang; Zhi-Kui Chen; Hai-Tao Yuan; Cheng Wang; Bing Han; Ping-Xi Xiao; Yi-Qiang Yuan; Zhen-Wen Yang; Liu Miao; Xiang Ma; Jian Yang; Dong-Fang You; Shao-Liang Chen; Jun-Jie Zhang; SEASON-AR Trial Investigators
abstract:
For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population.
We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year.
We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; P=0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure.
Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation.

title: Mitochondrial Metabolism-Related Candidate Signatures in Calcific Aortic Valve Disease Spectrum: An Exploratory Integrative Bioinformatics Study.
authors: Min Yang; Yingjing Gui; Hongbo Qian; Dafa Zhang
abstract: ​Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a progressive valvular disorder in which the role of mitochondrial metabolism remains incompletely understood. This exploratory study aimed to identify mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (MIMMRGs) associated with CAVD-spectrum valve remodeling. GSE83453 was used as the training dataset, and GSE51472 was used for expression-direction validation. Both datasets contain biologically and phenotypically heterogeneous groups of diseased valves. CAVD-associated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were integrated with MIMMRGs, followed by functional enrichment analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), expression validation, immune infiltration analysis, transcription factor analysis, drug and compound prediction, and molecular docking. A total of 909 DEGs and 1,234 MIMMRGs were identified, yielding 67 candidate genes enriched in metabolic and biosynthetic processes. ACADL and TDO2 were identified as candidate biomarkers and exhibited consistent expression differences between CAVD and normal samples in both datasets. Gene set enrichment analysis indicated the involvement of chemokine-related and immune-regulatory pathways. Four immune cell types differed between the CAVD and normal groups, and ACADL and TDO2 exhibited opposite correlations with naive B cells. HNF4A, STAT3, and AR were predicted to be common transcriptional regulators. Molecular docking indicated favorable in silico interactions between doxorubicin and ACADL and between dexamethasone and TDO2. In conclusion, ACADL and TDO2 are candidate biomarkers associated with mitochondrial metabolism and immune-related processes in heterogeneous CAVD-spectrum valve lesions. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and require independent clinical and experimental validation.

title: Paraparesis and left upper extremity weakness after total arch replacement with frozen elephant trunk: possible contributions of spinal cord ischaemia and cervical radiculopathy.
authors: Tomoaki Ishihama; Koki Yokawa; Yoshimitsu Shimatani; Kaede Uesugi; Ko Ishimoto; Tomonori Higuma; Kazunori Yoshida; Hidefumi Obo; Hidetaka Wakiyama
abstract: An 82-year-old man underwent total arch replacement with the frozen elephant trunk technique for an aortic arch aneurysm. Upon awakening 3 hours postoperatively, the patient exhibited flaccid paralysis of both lower extremities and left upper extremity weakness, whereas the right upper extremity was largely preserved. Cerebrospinal fluid drainage and blood pressure augmentation were initiated for suspected spinal cord ischemia. Lower-extremity motor function partially recovered, but left upper-extremity weakness persisted. Spinal magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated intramedullary T2 hyperintensity at T2/3 and bilateral neural foraminal stenosis from C3/4 to C6/7. Neurological examination revealed predominant weakness in the left C7 myotome with an absent left triceps reflexes, suggesting concomitant C7 radiculopathy. This case demonstrates that neurological deficits after aortic arch surgery may be multifactorial and highlights the value of detailed neurological examination and spinal imaging when upper extremity weakness is disproportionate.

title: Tissue Doppler S wave velocities are associated with changes in pro-brain natriuretic peptide levels following transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Sima Gharra; Gabby Elbaz-Greener; David Planer; Oren Yagel; David Leibowitz
journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an effective treatment for severe aortic stenosis. Despite its efficacy, TAVI carries risks of complications in elderly patients. Prior research indicates that failure to reduce NTproBNP levels post-TAVI increases the risk of mortality and recurrent hospitalizations. The tissue Doppler S wave is an index of longitudinal left ventricular function which may predict poor outcomes following TAVI.
The aim of the study was to examine whether pre-TAVI S wave velocities are associated with hemodynamic response to TAVI as assessed by changes in NTproBNP levels.
This prospective observational study enrolled patients scheduled for elective TAVI who underwent echocardiographic evaluation including TDI S wave measurements. Blood levels of NTproBNP were assessed both before and 3 months after the procedure. Subjects were defined as responders or non-responders (NR) with response defined as a ≥ 30% reduction in NTproBNP levels post-procedure.
185 subjects (mean age 79 ± 9 yrs., 47% male) were included in the study. Response to TAVI was observed in 78 (42%) of the cohort. The NR group had a significantly higher incidence of hypertension (62.3% vs. 37.7%, P = 0.017). Median S wave was 6.96 (3.8-13.7) cm/s in the responders and 5.88 (3.77-12.1) cm/s in the NR (p = 0.001), a finding which remained significant on multivariate analysis (p = 0.004; OR 1.31 95%CI 1.09-1.59).
This study demonstrates that for the first time that the TDI S wave is a significant predictor of NTproBNP reduction following TAVI. Further research is needed to validate these results in larger populations.

title: Prognostic value of pre- and post-procedural TAPSE/PASP ratio for long-term mortality in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction < 50% undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Aysel Akhundova; Berhan Keskin; Umeyir Savur; Aykun Hakgor; Özlem Önder; Fatih E Olgun; Atakan Dursun; Hacı M Güneş; Beytullah Çakal; Bilal Boztosun
journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
abstract:
Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE)/pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) ratio reflects right ventricular-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling and has prognostic value in heart failure and pulmonary hypertension. Its significance in patients with low ejection fraction (LVEF < 50%) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the association between pre-procedural TAPSE/PASP ratio and long-term all-cause mortality and to determine whether post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP ratio assessed at discharge was associated with subsequent mortality in patients with severe AS and LVEF < 50%.
This single-center retrospective study included 225 consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis and LVEF < 50% undergoing TAVI (2015-2025). TAPSE/PASP was measured at baseline and discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, analyzed using multivariable Cox regression.
Over a median follow-up of 1161 days, 102 (45.3%) patients died. Post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP was significantly higher in survivors (0.56 ±0.20 vs. 0.48 ±0.16 mm/mm Hg, p = 0.005) and was independently associated with long-term mortality (HR = 0.74 per 0.1 mm/mm Hg increase; 95% CI: 0.55-0.99; p = 0.04). Pre-TAVI TAPSE/PASP showed a borderline, non-significant association with mortality. Patients with post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP < 0.514 mm/mm Hg had significantly worse 5-year survival (log-rank p = 0.034).
In severe aortic stenosis with LVEF < 50%, post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP at discharge was independently associated with long-term mortality. The findings suggest that assessment of RV-PA coupling after TAVI may provide additional prognostic information, although the clinical utility of the proposed threshold requires prospective validation.

title: Changes in the institutional treatment of severe aortic stenosis following the introduction of transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Maja Rojko; Ema Kocjancic; Maja Kodra; Ales Pleskovic; Hrvoje Reschner; Matjaz Span; Nenad Danojevic; Miladin Ðordevic; Ninoslav Radovanovic; Metka Zorc; Stamenko Susak; Marko Noc
journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has transformed the treatment of severe aortic stenosis.
To investigate the association of TAVI introduction on institutional volume and characteristics of patients treated for aortic stenosis either by surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) or TAVI.
A single-centre retrospective observational study of consecutive patients treated only with SAVR (SAVR-only period, 2004-2017) and with either SAVR or TAVI (SAVR + TAVI period, 2017-2025).
During the SAVR-only period, 1011 patients underwent SAVR, and during the SAVR + TAVI period, 685 patients underwent SAVR and 824 underwent TAVI. The total number of aortic valve interventions increased annually by 9% (95% CI: 1.08-1.10; p < 0.001), while SAVR decreased by 15% during the SAVR + TAVI period (95% CI: 0.82-0.89; p < 0.001). Cumulative 30-day mortality was 2.8% during the SAVR-only period and 1.5% during the SAVR + TAVI period (p = 0.021). Patients undergoing SAVR during the SAVR + TAVI period were younger (68 vs. 70 years; p < 0.001), had a lower Logistic EuroSCORE (4.52 vs. 6.33; p < 0.001) and less often underwent concomitant revascularization (29% vs. 35%; p = 0.013). Patients undergoing TAVI compared to SAVR were older (80 vs. 68 years; p < 0.001), had a higher Logistic EuroSCORE (11.39 vs. 4.52; p < 0.001), and had comparable 30-day mortality (1.0% vs. 2.0%; p = 0.083). The difference in 5-year mortality in favour of SAVR (13.8% vs. 27.4%) was not significant after adjustment for age, sex and Logistic EuroSCORE (HR = 0.794; 95% CI: 0.550-1.147; p = 0.22).
Introduction of TAVI was associated with increased institutional volume of aortic valve interventions despite a concomitant decrease in the number of SAVR procedures. TAVI appears to have expanded treatment to previously undertreated high-risk elderly patients while also being used in a sizable proportion of patients who previously underwent SAVR.

title: Prognostic value of preprocedural neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio for in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced ejection fraction undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Kadir Biyikli; Mustafa Ferhat Keten; Nesri Danısman; Dogancan Ceneli; Can Erdem
journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
abstract:
Patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) represent a particularly vulnerable subgroup with elevated perioperative and long-term mortality. The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR), an integrated marker of systemic inflammation and nutritional status, has not been specifically evaluated as a prognostic marker in this population.
To examine the prognostic value of preprocedural NPAR for in-hospital and overall (all-cause) mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI.
This retrospective single-centre study enrolled 169 consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis and LVEF < 50% undergoing TAVI between June 2020 and January 2026. Preprocedural NPAR was derived from blood samples obtained within 24 h before the procedure. In-hospital and overall mortality were assessed using logistic and Cox regression models with limited covariate adjustment.
Using an NPAR cut-off of 20.74, patients with elevated NPAR exhibited higher rates of chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and both in-hospital and overall mortality, along with higher C-reactive protein and BNP levels and lower haemoglobin, albumin, postprocedural LVEF, and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) values. NPAR remained associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment for chronic kidney disease or TAPSE and was also associated with overall mortality in multivariable Cox regression analyses. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly reduced survival among patients with elevated NPAR.
After limited multivariable adjustment, preprocedural NPAR was associated with both in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI. As a simple marker of inflammatory and nutritional burden, NPAR may provide additional prognostic information and complement preprocedural risk assessment, although its incremental value beyond established risk models and other biomarkers remains uncertain.

title: Complex decision-making in severe bicuspid aortic stenosis after multiple thoracic interventions.
authors: Klaudia Piwowar; Łukasz Niewiara; Bogusław Kapelak; Paweł Kleczyński; Jacek Legutko; Jakub Podolec
journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology

title: Clinical and Genetic Characterization of a Patient With EED-Related Overgrowth Syndrome.
authors: Aidin Shahilooy; William T Gibson; Shermineh Heydari; Maryam Kiani; Amir Mohammad Roshanaie; Hamid Reza Moazzeni; Ahmad Reza Salehi Chaleshtori
abstract: Cohen-Gibson syndrome (COGIS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in EED. As the COGIS phenotypic spectrum remains incompletely characterized, additional cases help refine understanding of the condition. We evaluated a 37-year-old man with EED-related COGIS features, including overgrowth and intellectual disability. Genetic workup included karyotyping, FMR1 CGG-repeat expansion testing, whole-exome sequencing, and a familial segregation analysis, which identified the previously reported heterozygous pathogenic variant NM_003797.5:c.772C>T:p.His258Tyr. Clinical findings and medical history were recorded; birth parameters were obtained retrospectively from parental report due to lack of official documentation. Echocardiography revealed mild mitral valve regurgitation, alongside features uncommon in previously reported patients-normal adult weight, a long face, normal head circumference, normally spaced eyes, camptodactyly, no history of cryptorchidism, and a normal gait. Notably, the patient's father carried the same variant with reduced Sanger peak height, suggesting possible mosaicism. This case highlights potential phenotypic variability in COGIS, including the cardiac finding warranting further study, and underscores the implications of suspected paternal mosaicism for genetic counseling. Further quantitative assessment of mosaicism and cardiac evaluation in future studies could help better define the clinical spectrum of COGIS.

title: Posterior Leaflet Restoration for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: EXPLORE MR Results.
authors: Ulrich Schäfer; Alexandre Abizaid; Jeffrey J Popma; Nicolò Azzola Guicciardi; Alex Khairkhahan; Davie Campbell; Alexandra Bakall; Irakli Gogorishvili; Tamaz Shaburishvili; Archil Chukhrukidze; Kari Feldt; Fabio Sandoli de Brito
abstract:
Secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) contributes to morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic valve disease. Although transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is beneficial, many patients remain suboptimal candidates. Posterior leaflet restoration (PLR) provides a prosthetic coaptation surface via an adaptive coaptation element that inflates during systole and deflates during diastole to facilitate leaflet coaptation.
This study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of PLR using the MRace implant (Polares Medical, Inc).
Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant in Georgia and Brazil (EXPLORE MR) enrolled 78 symptomatic patients with severe secondary MR (≥3+), stratified post hoc by left ventricular end-diastolic volume: nonseverely enlarged left ventricle (NSELV) (N = 46) and severely enlarged left ventricle (SELV) (N = 32). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were MR reduction and functional outcomes.
The implant was successfully deployed in 96.2% of patients. All-cause mortality at 30 days was 6.4%. MR ≤2+ was achieved in 93.8% of patients at 30 days and was sustained in 90.6% at 1 year. Patients with NSELV showed better results in MR ≤1+ at every time point (94.4% at 30 days, 89.5% at 1 year) compared with the SELV group (79.3% and 69.2%, respectively). The NSELV subgroup demonstrated better functional recovery, with NYHA functional class I or II rising from 8.7% to 84.2%, vs a more attenuated response in the SELV group (15.6%-76.9%). The 6-minute walk test improved in the paired NSELV cohort (Δ +93.9 m), but not in paired patients with SELV (Δ -7.8 m). Kaplan-Meier 1-year all-cause mortality was 29.5% overall and was better in patients with NSELV (19.4%) than in SELV (41.7%).
PLR with the MRace implant achieves substantial MR reduction and meaningful functional improvement, most pronounced in patients without severely enlarged left ventricles. (XPLORE MRace [BR]: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant [EXPLORE MRace]; NCT06113354).

title: Libman-Sacks Endocarditis as the First Presentation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in a Young Man: A Multisystemic Diagnostic Challenge.
authors: Scott Waring; Joseph W Fletcher; Aaron Jones
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex, phenotypically varied disorder that possesses wide-ranging cardiac involvement. Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is one such cardiac manifestation, which results from the deposition of verrucous, sessile lesions favoring the left-sided heart valves. LSE is typically clinically silent without significant valvular dysfunction. Such patients with LSE, however, are those most susceptible to a more severe clinical phenotype resulting from SLE. Here, we report a unique case of a 22-year-old man initially presenting with unilateral leg swelling found to be secondary to a deep-vein thrombosis. He subsequently developed a constellation of acute symptoms, including embolic strokes, splenic infarction, proteinuric kidney injury, and significant mitral regurgitation, all of which mimicked bacterial endocarditis. His complex, multi-systemic disease course presented diagnostic challenges. We highlight the need in such complex cases for a specialist-led multidisciplinary approach, including cardiologists and rheumatologists, to guide serological and radiological investigations. Early use of echocardiography, in particular 3D transesophageal imaging, was paramount in clinching the diagnosis of LSE as an index presentation of SLE and in the transition from intravenous antibiotics to immunosuppression. Our case underscores the importance of the multidisciplinary team and the role of echocardiography in identifying such patients with LSE in SLE and thereby those most vulnerable to significant end-organ sequelae.

title: 3D Intracardiac Echocardiography-Guided Mitral M-TEER for a Challenging Medial P3 Flail in Patient With Esophagectomy.
authors: Karl Abou Zeid; Charishma Nallapati; Chloe Kharsa; Karl Aramouni; Selin Haci; Nadeen Faza; Stephen Little; Michael J Reardon; Sachin S Goel; Neal S Kleiman; Joe Aoun
abstract:
Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) is the standard imaging modality for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER). When TEE is contraindicated, 3-dimensional intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) may provide an alternative; however, published experience remains limited and has predominantly involved central A2/P2 pathology.
A 69-year-old man with severe degenerative MR from a medial P3 flail and prior esophagectomy underwent M-TEER exclusively under 2D/3D ICE guidance. ICE facilitated transseptal puncture, guide positioning, clip orientation, leaflet grasping, and assessment of residual MR and transmitral gradient. One MitraClip XTW was implanted at A3/P3, reducing MR from severe to mild with a mean gradient of 2 mm Hg. He was discharged the following day without complications.
This case demonstrates that comprehensive ICE guidance can extend M-TEER beyond the commonly reported A2/P2 position to challenging medial anatomy.
Comprehensive 2D and 3D ICE can enable safe and effective M-TEER of challenging A3-P3 pathology when TEE is contraindicated or not feasible.

title: Hemodynamic-Guided Management of Moderate Secondary Mitral Regurgitation and Chronic Heart Failure.
authors: Kyle Roter; JoAnn Lindenfeld; Kashish Goel; Sandip K Zalawadiya
abstract:
Contemporary guidelines recommend mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (mTEER) for patients with heart failure (HF) and moderate-to-severe or severe secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) who remain symptomatic despite optimal medical therapy. The benefits of mTEER in patients with chronic HF and moderate SMR are unclear.
A 65-year-old woman with chronic HF and moderate SMR underwent implantable pulmonary artery pressure sensor placement. Pulmonary artery diastolic pressures remained elevated (>20 mm Hg) despite diuretic escalations, and she was hospitalized for acute HF. She underwent mTEER, resulting in a sustained improvement in pulmonary artery diastolic pressure (≤20 mm Hg), functional class, subjective quality of life, and no further HF hospitalizations. WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES?: The SMR was moderate by echocardiography and would not have met guideline-supported severity criteria for mTEER.
Hemodynamic-guided management may help select patients with HF and moderate SMR who might benefit from mTEER.
Current guidelines do not establish a role for mTEER in patients with HF and moderate SMR who remain symptomatic despite optimal medical therapy. Longitudinal hemodynamic monitoring may support multidisciplinary assessment when symptoms and congestion appear disproportionate to SMR severity by echocardiography.

title: Targeted Transcatheter Mitral Edge-to-Edge Repair for Dynamic Systolic Anterior Motion After Mitral Valve Repair.
authors: Ibrahim Naoum; Juliana Perez Pinzon; Miles Shen; Melissa Todice; Marc Pelletier; Emmanuel Akintoye; Amit N Vora

title: Perioperative Care of Heart Failure, Arrhythmias, and Valvular Heart Disease.
authors: Avital Y O'Glasser; Efrén C Manjarrez
abstract: Frequently, the question of whether or not a patient is stable for surgery boils down to the question, "Does this patient need a preoperative stress test?" However, coronary artery disease and ischemic heart disease are only some of the many cardiac conditions that patients present with preoperatively-and that can negatively impact their intraoperative management and postoperative outcomes. This article will explore the evidence based, patient centered best practices surrounding the perioperative evaluation and management of heart failure, arrhythmias, and valvular heart disease.

title: Development and external validation of a preprocedural prediction model for 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Qi Chen; Thierry Donati; Monika Hebeisen; Florian A Wenzl; Neria E Winkler; Panagiotis Savvoulidis; Chantal Wohlwend; Jonathan Michel; Barbara Stähli; Albert M Kasel; Thomas F Lüscher; Felix C Tanner
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a well-established treatment for severe aortic stenosis but not recommended for patients with a life-expectancy below 1 year. Nevertheless, 1 year mortality after TAVI is around 15% in current reports. Accurate prediction models are thus needed to prevent futile interventions.
Patients undergoing TAVI were prospectively recruited between 2008 and 2021 from a single-centre registry in Zurich, Switzerland and data split into derivation and validation datasets. Four expert cardiologists defined relevant candidate predictors. A prediction model was developed using multiple logistic regression after imputation of missing data. An independent cohort undergoing TAVI from 2008 to 2018 in London, UK served as an external validation dataset. Performance of the prediction model was assessed through internal and external validation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and calibration plots were used for discrimination and calibration.
A total of 1702 patients were included from the Swiss cohort. Among these 1278 were used for model development and 424 for validation. 12 predictors were incorporated including age, male sex, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, haemoglobin, creatinine, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, troponin, left ventricular ejection fraction, mean transaortic pressure gradient and severe mitral regurgitation. The prediction model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.72 (95% CI 0.63 to 0.81) in internal validation and showed optimal sensitivity and specificity for 1-year mortality prediction at a probability threshold of 20%, outperforming European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II and Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS-PROM) score. In the external validation dataset consisting of 851 patients from the UK cohort, the AUC was 0.64 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.70).
The TAVI-specific risk model demonstrated acceptable performance for prediction of 1-year mortality after TAVI across two contemporary real-world cohorts, highlighting its potential for clinical application instead of EuroSCORE II or STS-PROM.

title: Posterior Mitral Leaflet Length and Outcomes After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: From The OCEAN-Mitral Registry.
authors: Sachiyo Ono; Shunsuke Kubo; Mikitaka Fujita; Naoki Nishiura; Kazunori Mushiake; Kohei Osakada; Takeshi Maruo; Mitsuru Abe; Masanori Yamamoto; Atsushi Sugiura; Tetsuro Shimura; Mike Saji; Masahiko Asami; Yusuke Enta; Shinichi Shirai; Masaki Izumo; Shingo Mizuno; Yusuke Watanabe; Yuki Izumi; Makoto Amaki; Kazuhisa Kodama; Hisao Otsuki; Daisuke Hachinohe; Toru Naganuma; Hiroki Bota; Yohei Ohno; Masahiro Yamawaki; Hiroshi Ueno; Gaku Nakazawa; Toshiaki Otsuka; Kentaro Hayashida; OCEAN-Mitral investigators
abstract:
A short posterior mitral leaflet (PML) length is challenging anatomy for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER); however, its prognostic impact remains unclear.
This study evaluated the association between PML length and M-TEER outcomes.
A total of 2,441 patients with functional mitral regurgitation (MR) were stratified by preprocedural PML length: very short (7 mm or less, n = 82), short (>7-10 mm, n = 736), and adequate (>10 mm, n = 1,623) groups. Procedural outcomes, echocardiographic data, and all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization were compared.
Median follow-up was 14.4 months [Q1-Q3: 10.2-27.5]. At discharge, MR grade 1+ or less was comparable among the 3 groups (very short: n = 63/82, 77% vs short: n = 598/736, 81% vs adequate: n = 1,259/1,623, 78%; P = 0.129). At 1 year, MR grade numerically worsened in the very short group (MR grade 1+ or less, n = 31/52, 60%). The rate of achieving both MR grade 1+ or less and transmitral mean pressure gradient <5 mm Hg was similar among groups at discharge, but it was significantly lower in the very short group (n = 14/39, 36%) than in the short (n = 201/306, 66%) and adequate (n = 440/665, 66%) groups (P < 0.001) at 1 year. Although the incidence of the composite outcome was higher in shorter groups (P = 0.018), the PML length was not an independent risk factor in the multivariate analysis.
M-TEER may be feasible in selected patients with shorter PML; however, very short PML might have less favorable echocardiographic durability, warranting anatomical assessment and follow-up. Given the small subgroup and limited follow-up, these findings require cautious interpretation and validation.
OCEAN-Mitral registry (UMIN000023653).

title: Clinical Impact of Multiple-Clip Implantation for Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
authors: Takashi Nagasaka; Vivek Patel; Kazuki Suruga; Hidemasa Shitan; Yuchao Guo; Ofir Koren; Alon Shechter; Dhairya Patel; Tarun Chakravarty; Aakriti Gupta; Hideki Ishii; Hasan Jilaihawi; Moody Makar; Mamoo Nakamura; Raj R Makkar
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
Residual moderate or greater mitral regurgitation (MR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the prognostic impact of implanting additional clips in patients with significant residual MR after the first clip remains uncertain. We evaluated the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of multiple-clip implantation for significant residual MR following placement of the initial clip.
We retrospectively evaluated 826 patients with moderate or greater residual MR on intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiography after placement of the first clip during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center from 2014 to 2023. Patients were categorized into single-clip (n=113) and multiple-clip (n=713) groups. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year.
Procedural technical success and complication rates were comparable between groups. The multiple-clip group demonstrated greater MR reduction and higher transmitral pressure gradients at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. At 1 year, the composite end point occurred less frequently in the multiple-clip group than in the single-clip group (16.8% versus 29.2%; P=0.002), along with greater and more sustained improvement in New York Heart Association functional class. In subgroup analyses, multiple-clip implantation consistently reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with moderate as well as moderate-severe/severe residual MR.
In patients with significant residual MR after implanting the first clip, multiple-clip implantation improved MR reduction and 1-year outcomes without increasing complications. Even in moderate residual MR, additional clips were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes.

title: Unilateral pulmonary oedema secondary to acute severe mitral regurgitation mimicking pneumonia: A case report.
authors: Elsayed Khalil; Mohamed Abada; Ahmed Hamada
abstract: Unilateral pulmonary oedema is a rare and frequently under-recognized manifestation of acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema. Its unilateral radiographic appearance often mimics pneumonia, leading to diagnostic delay, and inappropriate initial management. Acute severe mitral regurgitation is among the most important cardiac causes of unilateral pulmonary oedema, particularly when associated with eccentric regurgitant jets directed toward the pulmonary veins.

title: Stuck in the Traffic-Light: Moving Past Color Signals to Real Decisions in Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Therapy Management.
authors: Vratika Agarwal; Firas Zahr
journal: Structural heart : the journal of the Heart Team
abstract: Historically, the complexity of patients being evaluated for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge therapy (M-TEER) has been divided into 3 main categories: green zone: defined as cases where M-TEER is straightforward and not complex, yellow zone: cases with medium complexity where M-TEER is feasible but not entirely straightforward, and red zone: cases where you would not consider M-TEER as the first option and may be swayed toward consideration of other options like transcatheter mitral valve (MV) replacement or surgical management. However, the advancement in preprocedural planning with precise anatomical definition by 3-dimensional imaging modalities has changed how we address complex mitral regurgitation cases. The expansion of available devices for management of MV disease has changed the way we think about undertaking challenging M-TEER procedures. Management in the current era emphasizes meticulous preprocedural assessment of mitral regurgitation pathology, strategic planning for device implantation, judicious device choice, and early consideration of transcatheter MV replacement or other innovative transcatheter devices. This review article provides a comprehensive overview of the available data on M-TEER and outlines treatment strategies for complex cases within the context of contemporary transcatheter technologies.

title: Beyond mortality prediction after mitral TEER: Which risks remain modifiable?
authors: Teruhiko Imamura
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions

title: Serum fibroblast growth factor-23 concentration in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease.
authors: Naoki Iwasa; Mamu Shimizu; Tomoko Okamoto; Hiroto Kosuga; Nayu Morikita; Mifumi Kawabe; Munetaka Iwata; Kazuhiro Watanabe; Yui Kobatake; Satoshi Takashima; Naohito Nishii
abstract:
Circulating fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF-23) is primarily a kidney-related biomarker, but also may be influenced by cardiovascular remodeling and hemodynamic load.
Verify whether serum FGF-23 concentration increases with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) severity.
Forty-two client-owned dogs with MMVD without overt kidney disease.
Retrospective cross-sectional study to evaluate serum FGF-23, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine (Cr), and symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) concentrations. Imaging variables included vertebral heart score (VHS), vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), left atrial-to-aortic root ratio (LA/Ao), normalized left-ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDDN), and diastolic transmitral E-wave velocity (E-vel). Differences among American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine stages were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Correlations were analyzed using Spearman's correlation. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with serum FGF-23 concentration.
Dogs with ACVIM stages C and D had higher serum FGF-23 concentrations than those with stages B1 and B2 (P < .05). Serum FGF-23 concentrations were positively correlated with VLAS (rs = 0.500, P < .01), ANP (rs = 0.455, P < .01), LA/Ao (rs = 0.384, P < .05), E-vel (rs = 0.372, P < .05), and NT-proBNP (rs = 0.366, P < .05). ACVIM stage was significantly associated with serum FGF-23 concentration after adjustment for serum Cr concentration and loop diuretic use.
The potential influence of MMVD should be considered when interpreting increased circulating FGF-23 concentrations in dogs with MMVD.

title: Severe Hypercoagulability With Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis After KRAS Inhibitor Exposure: A Perfect Storm.
authors: Cecilia Villa-Etchegoyen; Raymond B Fohtung; Kwan S Lee; Chadi Ayoub; Reza Arsanjani
abstract:
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) is a rare malignancy-associated condition causing systemic embolization and valvular dysfunction. Its presentation as new severe mitral regurgitation (MR) may be difficult to recognize.
A 76-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma developed progressive dyspnea after treatment with the KRAS inhibitor daraxonrasib. Echocardiography demonstrated new severe MR with leaflet thickening and broad-based echodensities. His course was complicated by pulmonary embolism, recurrent coronary thrombosis, and persistently negative blood cultures. Transesophageal echocardiography confirmed bilateral leaflet involvement with a central coaptation defect. Anticoagulation was changed to low-molecular-weight heparin.
NBTE should be considered in patients with malignancy presenting with new MR and thrombotic events without evidence of infection. The temporal association with KRAS inhibition is noteworthy but does not establish causality.
NBTE may present as subacute MR. Echocardiography and clinical context are essential for timely diagnosis and management.

title: Can the QTc interval and T-wave morphology change intermittently in arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse? First paediatric case experience.
authors: Senem Özgür; Serpil Kaya Çelebi; Selman Kesici; Murat Akkus; Yakup Ergul
abstract:
Mitral valve prolapse is typically considered a benign condition. However, a newly described repolarisation anomaly known as arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome is closely associated with repolarisation disturbances and can potentially lead to sudden cardiac death. Arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome is characterised by bileaflet mitral valve prolapse, mitral valve regurgitation, T-wave inversions in the inferolateral leads, and complex ventricular ectopy.
In this case, we present the diagnosis of arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome in a 16-year-old adolescent girl who experienced sudden cardiac arrest during exercise. Her electrocardiograms revealed intermittent QT/QTc prolongation. Interestingly, QT prolongation was always associated with T wave inversion in inferolateral leads. Heterozygous genomic changes were detected in the KCNH2 gene and the 25th exon of the ANK2 gene. These findings support the diagnosis of arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse syndrome in this patient.
Since mitral valve prolapse is a common condition in the society, it is important to determine beforehand which ones are at risk of sudden death. As these boundaries are drawn better, underdiagnosis as well as overdiagnosis will be prevented.

title: When Transcatheter Mitral Repair Meets Cor Triatriatum Sinistrum.
authors: Aniela Monica Popescu

title: Decompensated heart failure after one year of successful therapy with mavacamten: a case report.
authors: Giulia Marchionni; Lucrezia Netti; Silvia Stavagna; Cristina Chimenti
abstract:
Cardiac myosin inhibition is the first disease-specific therapeutic strategy for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Mavacamten, the first-in-class agent, has demonstrated an excellent safety profile and sustained efficacy in both clinical trials and real-world practice. However, its safe use requires careful monitoring and thorough patient education regarding potential drug-drug interactions.
We report a case of acute heart failure occurring after long-term clinical stability on mavacamten following concomitant fluconazole administration. It is reasonable to assume that the pharmacokinetic interaction resulted in excessive mavacamten exposure, leading to transient systolic dysfunction, severe functional mitral regurgitation, and adverse left ventricular remodelling.
This case report highlights the consequences of pharmacological interactions between mavacamten and a strong CYP2C19 inhibitor. Drug-drug interaction should always be considered and systematically excluded in a patient presenting with unexplained heart failure and left ventricular remodelling during mavacamten therapy.

title: Sotagliflozin improves mitral regurgitation symptoms in rats.
authors: Jorge Ferreira

title: Deep learning-based genetic disease prediction with Monte Carlo (MC) dropout uncertainty estimation: a comparative study with classical machine learning baselines.
authors: V S Keerthana; Tarak Hussain
abstract:
Deep neural networks have been successfully applied to structured clinical data with a good predictive performance, but their point predictions do not reflect an indication of confidence, which limits their trustworthiness in screening for genetic conditions where an overconfident misclassification may delay the appropriate confirmatory testing or intervention.
A feed-forward neural network (128-64-32 hidden units, batch normalization, and dropout p = 0.3) was trained to classify patients into five genetic-disease-associated groups based on twelve regularly accessible clinical and molecular biomarkers, using a publicly available, pre-labelled structured biomedical dataset (n = 1,000) whose real-world clinical vs. synthetic provenance could not be independently confirmed (see Section 2.1 and Limitations). Performance was assessed using stratified 5-fold cross-validation versus four traditional baselines (logistic regression, random forest, SVM, gradient boosting; McNemar's test for pairwise significance). We quantified predictive uncertainty using Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout (T up to 200 stochastic passes), decomposed it into epistemic and aleatoric components, and evaluated it thru calibration analysis (ECE, MCE, Brier score, negative log-likelihood), an uncertainty-quality analysis (low/medium/high uncertainty strata), a selective-prediction (risk-coverage) analysis, a seven-configuration ablation study, and robustness testing across random seeds, reduced training data, and Gaussian feature noise. Results The developed network achieved 94.30% +- 1.36% cross-validated accuracy which was statistically comparable to logistic regression (p = 0.092) and gradient boosting (p = 0.238) but considerably inferior to random forest (95.50% +- 1.26%, p = 0.0018) and SVM (95.30% +- 1.36%, p = 0.0063). MC-Dropout obtained 93.33% accuracy (macro F1 = 0.933, macro ROC-AUC = 0.971, MCC = 0.917) with ECE = 0.076 on a held-out test partition-numerically the highest (worst) ECE among the six model/inference configurations evaluated, exceeding all four classical baselines (ECE 0.024-0.066), although MC-Dropout inference reduced negative log-likelihood substantially relative to deterministic inference (0.370 vs. 0.445), indicating its calibration benefit is concentrated in reducing the penalty for confident errors rather than in bin-wise confidence-accuracy alignment. Errors were about twice as likely in the highest (most uncertain) tercile of predictions than in the lowest (12.0% vs. 6.0% mistake rate), and 60% of all misclassifications were within the high-uncertainty group. Removing the most doubtful 20%-30% of predictions yielded a retained-sample accuracy of above 95%. Accuracy and calibration were consistent across five random seeds (93.07%) and deteriorated gracefully with increasing predictive entropy under synthetic feature-noise perturbation.
On this structured, moderate-sized genetic-disease benchmark dataset-evaluated entirely through internal computational validation, without external or prospective clinical testing-classical machine learning algorithms achieved statistically comparable or slightly higher raw classification accuracy than this deep learning approach under standard, non-tuned hyperparameters for all models.

title: AI-integrated Approaches in Alzheimer's Disease: Linking Molecular Pathways, Biomarkers, and Emerging Therapies.
authors: Namra Aziz; Kritika Sachan; Anuradha Singh; Sakshi Srivastava; Pranay Wal; Rajesh Gupta; Krishana Kumar Sharma; Amin Gasmi
abstract:
Alzheimer's disease (AD) continues to be the leading cause of dementia worldwide, due to its complicated, multifactorial pathophysiology. To shift the AD paradigm from reactive to proactive, from a specific time to a precision medicine intervention strategy, this study examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) as a potential linking point for multi-omics data, new fluid biomarkers, and developing medicines.
A thorough search was conducted in clinical trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov) and peerreviewed literature (PubMed, Scopus). Without going too far into detail, this study discussed novel anti-amyloid/anti-tau monoclonal antibody treatments, blood biomarkers (p-tau217, p-tau181), and machine learning approaches for early diagnostic classification and for prediction modelling.
Recent breakthroughs in understanding that different disease-modifying treatments, such as lecanemab and donanemab, can stop cognitive decline by targeting specific types of disease-causing aggregates have greatly shortened diagnostic time through blood-based diagnostic markers. Importantly, AI systems (e.g., structural MRI and multi-omics-based panels analyzed using Deep Learning architectures) can predict conversion from Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) to overt AD more than a year before the onset of clinical symptoms, with accuracy exceeding 90%. Sensitivity of real-world trials is significantly enhanced by the use of Digital Biomarkers and remote cognitive monitoring.
As a tool, AI is not discrete but serves as a coherent framework that can progressively connect data from different biological systems (e.g., upstream molecular events such as amyloid cascades, tauopathy, neuroinflammation) with downstream clinical events (phenotypes). The lack of standardized datasets across different ethnic groups, algorithm interpretability (the "black box" problem), and possible regulatory validation, however, is now preventing the full clinical translation.
With insulin injections, or even just the excitement of a new drug, the world of AD research is transformed. The multimodal AI frameworks provide clinicians with ways to treat patients with highly personalized, multi-targeted treatment strategies to capture AD pathology at its asymptomatic early stage, by simultaneously computing genetic risk, neuroimaging features, and plasma biomarker levels.

title: Long-Term Predictive Value of MRI Radiomics in Identifying Patients with Metastasis-Free Breast Cancer Over a 100-Month Follow-Up Period: A retrospective, observational study.
authors: Yi-Shan Zhao; Yu Ji; Yan-Bo Li; Yu-Heng Wang; Xiao-Xu Ma; Jing-Bo Wang; Ping Wang; Hong Lu
abstract:
Postoperative distant metastasis remains a major challenge in breast cancer management, which significantly affects long-term survival among patients. Standard follow-up protocols rely on frequent imaging and clinical evaluations to detect recurrence early. However, such intensive surveillance imposes a financial and psychological burden on both patients and healthcare systems. Recent advances in breast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based radiomics provide new opportunities to capture tumor heterogeneity and may enhance individualized risk prediction. This study aims to assess the long-term predictive value of MRI-based radiomics combined with clinicopathological features in identifying patients with breast cancer and to investigate the potential of this approach in guiding individualized follow-up strategies.
This retrospective study included 388 women with breast cancer who underwent breast MRI between February 2015 and October 2017 at the Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute & Hospital. Radiomic features were extracted from tumor segmentations on second-phase dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) images using semiautomated and deep learning-based segmentation algorithms. The radiomic signature was constructed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) method and further integrated with clinical features, including tumor size, estrogen receptor (ER) status, and histological type, to develop ensemble machine learning models. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and additional metrics.
The combined radiomics-clinical model yielded an AUC of 0.686 for predicting distant metastasis over a 100-month follow-up period in the validation cohort. A predicted probability of 0.22-the lowest value observed among metastatic cases-was used as the risk threshold. Approximately one-third of nonmetastatic patients (n = 32) fell below this cutoff, and all remained metastasis-free during follow-up. ER and Progesterone Receptor (PR) positivity were significantly more common in this subgroup compared to those with a higher predicted risk or confirmed metastasis (ER, p < .005; PR, p < .005).
Radiomics-based modeling using DCE-MRI and clinical data demonstrated potential in effectively predicting long-term metastatic risk in patients with breast cancer and identifying a subset of metastatic-free patients with favorable profiles who may benefit from less intensive surveillance.

title: Artificial Intelligence-integrated Multimodal Neural Biomarkers for Early Risk Stratification in Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease.
authors: G M Savitha Mol; Antony Justin; D Uma Maheswari; Gomathi Vengatachalam
abstract:
Alzheimer's Disease (AD) develops biologically years before overt cognitive symptoms, creating a need for preclinical risk stratification beyond single biomarker tests.
This structured narrative review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for English-language literature published from 2009 to July 2026 on preclinical AD, multimodal biomarkers, and AI-based risk prediction. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively; PRISMA was not applied because the review was not systematic.
Individual biomarkers provide complementary but incomplete signals and are limited by biological discordance, temporal heterogeneity, mixed pathologies, cost, invasiveness, and variable clinical availability. Machine learning, deep learning, graph neural networks, and transformer- based models can integrate heterogeneous data, model longitudinal trajectories, and estimate individual risk of amyloid or tau positivity, cognitive decline, and clinical conversion.
Clinical translation requires longitudinal and externally validated datasets, standardized assays and imaging pipelines, population-specific calibration, transparent reporting, management of missing data and bias, privacy protection, and workable clinical integration.
Multimodal AI can shift AD assessment from late symptom-based diagnosis toward scalable, biologically informed, patient-specific preclinical risk prediction, supporting biomarker triage, trial enrichment, and future clinical decision-making.

title: Free-breathing fast abdominal simultaneous T1, T2, PD and B1 mapping via deep learning reconstruction.
authors: Yuchen Zheng; Weikun Chen; Qing Lin; Taishan Kang; Xiaobo Qu; Liuhong Zhu; Zhiliang Wei; Liangjie Lin; Jianzhong Lin; Zhong Chen; Jianfa Chen; Shuhui Cai; Jianjun Zhou; Qin Lin; Congbo Cai
abstract:
Multi-parametric quantitative MRI (mqMRI) enables non-invasive tissue characterization and holds significant clinical value in abdominal imaging. Conventional methods are restricted by long acquisition times and motion artifacts induced by physiological processes and irregular breathing, leading to registration errors between sequential acquisitions.
To develop and evaluate a framework for abdominal quantitative imaging under free-breathing conditions with reduced scan time and improved robustness to motion.
A novel framework integrating the longitudinal magnetization-controlled multiple overlapping-echo detachment (LMC-MOLED) sequence with synthetic data-driven deep learning reconstruction was proposed. To generate the synthetic dataset for training, a respiratory motion model combining global and local displacement vector fields was developed, ensuring temporal alignment with the inter-phase intervals of LMC-MOLED acquisitions. By applying interpolation to the original template, virtual imaging objects were generated to simulate respiratory-induced deformations while preserving anatomical textures, tissue boundaries, and inter-slice correlations. These objects were subsequently processed with MRI Bloch simulation to generate the final synthetic dataset, which was used to train a BGA-Multi-UNet architecture for motion correction and improved quantitative accuracy.
The proposed framework enabled simultaneous mapping of T1, T2, proton density, and B1 under free-breathing conditions. With a 5-slice interleaved acquisition, the average acquisition time was reduced to approximately one second per slice without the need for respiratory gating. Both numerical and in vivo experiments demonstrated high accuracy and repeatability, with image quality comparable to conventional breath-hold acquisitions while mitigating motion-induced artifacts.
This framework offers a rapid and reliable solution for multi-parametric abdominal imaging under free-breathing conditions. The combination of synthetic motion modeling with deep learning reconstruction enables accurate quantitative mapping with effective motion correction, offering potential clinical benefits for efficient and robust abdominal magnetic resonance imaging.

title: Reliability-weighted patch learning for synthetic CT reconstruction in head and neck adaptive radiotherapy: A proof-of-concept study.
authors: Jeong Heon Kim; Sven Olberg; Byong Su Choi; Sridhar Yaddanapudi; Xiaoying Liang; Bo Lu; Jun Tan; Jin Sung Kim; So Hyun Ahn; Keith M Furutani; Chris J Beltran; Justin C Park
abstract:
Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is essential for adaptive radiotherapy (ART) but is limited by poor image quality. Existing deep learning methods for synthetic CT (sCT) generation face a critical trade-off: diffusion models offer high fidelity but are impractically slow, while fast-inference networks often lack structural accuracy and optimization stability.
To develop HQ-PatchNet, a reliability-driven deep learning framework designed to improve CBCT-to-sCT image quality while maintaining rapid inference speed for online ART workflows.
HQ-PatchNet utilizes a vision transformer (ViT)-integrated CycleGAN architecture. It introduces a reliability-driven, SSIM-based selective patch weighting mechanism controlled by a temperature decay schedule. This dynamically suppresses artifact-dominated regions and focuses optimization on anatomically reliable structures. The model was evaluated on 304 paired head-and-neck (HN) scans against conventional networks and recent diffusion models using quantitative metrics (MAE, SSIM, NCC, PSNR), computational speed, and clinical dosimetric accuracy (3D gamma index, 2%/2 mm).
HQ-PatchNet improved image quality, reducing Mean Absolute Error (MAE) from 44.81 ± 11.24 HU to 11.85 ± 4.31 HU and achieving an SSIM of 0.960 ± 0.055, comparable to state-of-the-art diffusion models. Inference required only 6.42 ± 1.71 s per volume, compared to > 15 min for diffusion approaches. The model reduced severe metal and truncation artifacts, and representative qualitative assessment suggested visually consistent sCT generation under interfractional anatomical variation. Dosimetric assessment of complex HN IMRT plans yielded a high average gamma passing rate of 99.32 ± 0.56%.
HQ-PatchNet provides a computationally efficient and clinically promising approach for daily CBCT-guided online ART by improving CBCT-to-sCT image quality while maintaining rapid inference speed. Further contour-based, multi-institutional, and multi-site validation remains necessary to confirm its broader clinical utility.

title: Deliberate Vulnerability at the Bedside: Operationalising Failure Rounds in Clinical Teaching.
authors: Sara Heydari; Reza Bidaki
abstract: Bedside rounds frequently devolve into performative clinical demonstrations where cognitive friction, uncertainty and diagnostic hesitations are masked by learners. Inspired by the AMEE 2026 symposium on "Failure Rounds," this perspective translates the pedagogical concept of deliberate vulnerability into front-line bedside clinical teaching. Grounded in psychological safety, productive failure and error-based learning frameworks, deliberate vulnerability repositions uncertainty from a professional deficit into a catalyst for diagnostic reasoning. Front-line faculty discussions highlight practical barriers, including safeguarding patient trust and balancing efficiency with deep pedagogical exploration. We propose three actionable, nonprescriptive pillars for clinical teachers: taking the first turn by acknowledging doubt, decoupling immediate patient care from cognitive debriefing and conducting structured micro-debriefings.

title: Contextual Semantic Pattern Recognition for Mental Health Monitoring Using ClinicalBERT Transformers.
authors: Junjun Sun
abstract:
