This study aimed to develop an interpretable ClinicalBERT-based framework for mental health monitoring using structured clinical data.
Because the Mental Health Diagnosis and Treatment Monitoring dataset contains structured patient attributes rather than free-text clinical narratives, a structured-to-text transformation module was used to convert the records into contextual descriptions suitable for ClinicalBERT. The proposed model was compared with Random Forest, XGBoost, Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), TabTransformer, and a Deep Neural Network, and to strengthen the experimental comparison, contemporary tabular transformer models, including SAINT and FT-Transformer, were also evaluated. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Cross-validation, confidence interval analysis, statistical significance testing, and ablation experiments were conducted to examine the reliability of the results. SHAP and LIME were used to explain global feature contributions and individual predictions.
ClinicalBERT achieved an accuracy of 90.2%, a precision of 90.5%, a recall of 90.4%, and an F1-score of 90.6%, outperforming all comparison models. The additional validation analyses supported the stability of the results. SHAP and LIME further identified the patient attributes that contributed most strongly to the model's predictions.
The findings indicate that structured clinical records can be transformed into contextual representations for transformer-based mental health monitoring. The framework combines predictive performance with interpretable output, although its evaluation is currently limited to a single dataset. Further validation using multi-institutional and prospective data is required.

title: OGRR-Net: observation-guided residual refinement learning for photoacoustic imaging.
authors: Qi Liu; Fengchen Luo; Hengrong Lan; Fei Gao; Siyu Liu
abstract: Photoacoustic imaging provides optical-absorption contrast through ultrasonic detection. However, image reconstruction remains affected by acquisition geometry, detector response, acoustic noise, and the attenuation of high-frequency components during analytic inversion. Although deep post-processing methods have shown effectiveness in artifact reduction, purely image-domain restoration lacks a direct mechanism for incorporating complementary information contained in the raw measurement data. This work proposes OGRR-Net, an observation-guided residual refinement network for photoacoustic imaging. The network takes an initial reconstruction as the spatial reference and encodes the corresponding raw sinogram into an observation-guidance map, which conditions a gated residual correction pathway for image refinement. Evaluated on an in vivo mouse dataset and the OADAT optoacoustic dataset against representative image-domain and hybrid reconstruction methods, the proposed observation-guided strategy improves reconstruction fidelity, reduces artifacts, and enhances the preservation of structural details.

title: Binary deep prior guided video snapshot compressive imaging for full-field displacement measurement.
authors: Mengxi Qin; Xiaohui Wei; Haibo Liu
abstract: High-speed full-field displacement measurement is constrained by the cost of high-speed cameras and the trade-off between frame rate and spatial resolution. Video snapshot compressive imaging (SCI) reconstructs multiple frames from a single exposure, offering an effective route to low-cost high-speed displacement measurement. Among SCI reconstruction methods, plug-and-play (PnP)-based methods offer favorable theoretical interpretability and flexibility, and therefore hold great promise for high-speed imaging applications such as photomechanical measurement. However, they typically adopt full-precision deep networks as the denoising prior, and this cost becomes significant in high-resolution, resource-constrained measurement systems. To address this issue, we propose a binary deep prior guided snapshot compressive imaging for full-field displacement measurement, termed BDPnP. Specifically, to the best of our knowledge, we first propose a lightweight deep video denoiser as an implicit prior based on binary convolutions, which significantly reduces the computational complexity and parameter count. Building upon this, a cross-measurement temporal collaboration strategy and a hybrid prior alternating strategy are proposed to alleviate temporal-context fragmentation at measurement boundaries and performance degradation under non-ideal hardware imaging, respectively. These two strategies further compensate for the information loss from binarization. Finally, we constructed an SCI hardware system and integrated BDPnP with a digital image correlation pipeline, using rigid-body translation as a benchmark case with exactly known ground truth. At 1024 × 1024 resolution with a compression ratio of 8, i.e., an eightfold gain in the effective acquisition frame rate, BDPnP achieves a mean displacement error of 0.045 mm, only 0.34% of the total displacement. This is comparable to the lowest mean error achieved by the fine-tuned deep learning method in our experiments (0.044 mm) while requiring only 1/47.7 of its FLOPs and 1/7.7 of its parameters. Our code is available at https://github.com/hnu-VML/qmx/tree/main/BDPnP.

title: Intelligent intrinsic physical layer security: joint authentication and encryption for data center communications.
authors: Xinshuai Liang; Chongfu Zhang; Yue Lin; Yuchi Tian; Jiao Du; Wenjun Zeng
abstract: Navigating the era of artificial intelligence and massive cloud computing presents a critical challenge: securing the explosive growth of data traffic across optical data center interconnects (DCIs). However, conventional physical-layer security (PLS) methods often treat encryption and authentication as disjointed modules, lacking the intelligent adaptability for dynamic channels. Here, we propose an intelligent intrinsic PLS framework to jointly execute identity authentication and data encryption in short-reach DCIs. Enabled by end-to-end deep learning, this scheme integrates a mixture density network (MDN) for dynamic channel condition with a constellation autoencoder. Utilizing chaotic index modulation, the system nonlinearly learns highly distinguishable geometric constellations and embeds watermarks into subcarrier indices for redundancy-free transmission. Through this intelligent mapping, security attributes are natively fused into the physical signals. We achieve a secure transmission using discrete multi-tone (DMT) signaling over a 10-km standard single-mode fiber (SSMF). The results demonstrate that our scheme dynamically optimizes watermark embedding, strongly thwarting unauthorized eavesdropping and robustly resisting impersonation attacks. This avant-garde paradigm offers a highly scalable and intelligent solution for secure next-generation optical DCI networks.

title: Unsupervised geometric classifier based on optical feature extraction.
authors: Chengwen Huang; Junhe Zhou
abstract: Diffractive deep neural networks (D2NNs) offer extraordinary advantages for applications in real-time object classification, computational imaging, and optical computing, where speed and energy efficiency are critical. Unsupervised learning reduces reliance on labeled data, enhances robustness, and is inherently compatible with optical parallel processing. In this work, an unsupervised geometric classifier combining optical feature extraction and clustering is proposed. A D2NN processor trained on the Laguerre-Gaussian modes serves as an optical encoder, mapping the input fields to a six-dimensional feature space. Circles, along with randomly rotated triangles, squares, and pentagons, are modulated onto the phase of a Gaussian beam. After the modulated beams pass through the D2NN-based encoder, the resulting feature vectors enable unsupervised classification via clustering. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of unsupervised classification of different geometric shapes based on optical feature extraction. The experimental results show 100% classification accuracy for the four different geometric shapes, including circles and randomly rotated triangles, squares, and pentagons.

title: Deep learning-empowered metasurface design for complex target ISAR illusions.
authors: Cheng Zhu; Shaozhong Fu; Wang Xu; Jiayue He; Yuanyuan Li; Bowen Ma
abstract: Scattering signature manipulation enabling advanced radar camouflage remains constrained in practical applications by narrow operational bandwidths, incidence-angle sensitivity, and complex analytical phase computations for geometric targets. To address these limitations, we report an inverse-design framework for the broadband inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image reconstruction of complex targets with different scattering characteristics, bypassing analytical phase derivations. The wideband phase distribution is extracted directly from the target's near-field electric field, and a cascaded forward-backward neural network is subsequently deployed to synthesize the corresponding meta-atom and array profiles. Employing the optimized metasurface, we achieve high-fidelity ISAR image illusions with a range resolution of 37.5 mm and a cross-range resolution of 15 mm across the 8-12 GHz band (X-band). The framework is validated through the broadband ISAR reconstruction of both a cross-section-invariant split metal plate and a cross-section-variant tower model, offering a robust approach for generating electromagnetic illusions of complex targets.

title: FCM-Encoder: a novel interpretable framework with vision-language reasoning for coronary artery disease and solitary pulmonary nodule classification.
authors: Anna Feleki; Elpiniki Papageorgiou; Ioannis D Apostolopoulos; Dimitris J Apostolopoulos; Nikolaos Papathanasiou; Nikolaos I Papandrianos
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
abstract: Although modern machine-learning models attain strong predictive performance, their clinical adoption remains limited by a lack of transparency. This concern is particularly relevant in multimodal diagnostic pipelines, where the contribution of each modality to the final prediction is more difficult to discern. Relatively few studies integrate heterogeneous clinical and imaging data, where they typically employ decision- or feature-level fusion, and provide limited insight into the cross-modal interactions that underline the diagnostic decision. We propose a Fuzzy Cognitive Map Encoder (FCM-Encoder) framework for multimodal explainable classification. Imaging features extracted by a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) are mapped into low-dimensional concepts and combined with normalised clinical concept activations inside a unified FCM. The connections to the diagnostic output are initialised from the Spearman rank correlation of each concept with the label, and all interconnections are then refined by a particle swarm optimisation strategy enhanced with Lévy-flight exploration. Under 10-fold cross-validation, the framework reached 81.82% ± 4.51% accuracy for Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) from clinical variables and polar maps, and 93.39% ± 3.09% for Solitary Pulmonary Nodule (SPN) classification in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) from CT, PET, and clinical data. The ablation analysis confirmed that each component contributes to the overall performance, the image-encoder comparison showed that the selected encoder matches or exceeds substantially larger pretrained backbones, and the graph-baseline comparison demonstrated that the FCM-based reasoning surpasses graph neural networks. FCM-Encoder further links imaging concepts to clinical labels and generates clinically aligned narratives through a Vision-Language module.

title: Detecting misconception surges in opioid policy: a zero-shot LLM analysis of British Columbia's decriminalization pilot.
authors: Zahra Shakeri; Marwa Sharifi; Sepehr Harfi Moridani; Chan Pang Yang; Konrad Samsel; Christoffer Dharma; Mohammad Noaeen
abstract:
In January 2023, British Columbia (BC) launched Canada's first drug decriminalization pilot in response to persistently high opioid-related deaths. This initiative removed criminal penalties for possession of up to 2.5 grams of certain illicit drugs to reduce stigma and increase service use. Social media platforms such as Reddit provide a real-time window into public perceptions and misconceptions about such policies.
We analyzed [Formula: see text] Reddit comment records posted between January 2023 and October 2024 from subreddits discussing decriminalization in British Columbia. A zero-shot large language model applied a multi-label taxonomy with four misconception classes and one no-claim class. Expert review of [Formula: see text] comments with model disagreement supported selection of the primary classifier for analysis. We tracked monthly misconception prevalence and used subreddit-week reply premiums and lattice clustering to detect engagement bursts. Negative binomial models quantified reply differences across periods, regions, and comment-level harm reduction references.
GPT-4o assigned at least one substantive misconception label to [Formula: see text] comment records ([Formula: see text]). Label 5 was assigned to [Formula: see text] records ([Formula: see text]), consistent with a conservative taxonomy that separates checkable policy claims from opinion, sarcasm, anecdote, and moral judgment. After the May 2024 amendment that restricted possession in public spaces, legal status and enforcement misconceptions increased. Legal or enforcement misconception records had a higher adjusted reply-rate estimate than other records, although the main effect had limited precision (IRR [Formula: see text], 95% CI [Formula: see text]-[Formula: see text], [Formula: see text]). The post-May interaction was positive (IRR [Formula: see text], 95% CI [Formula: see text]-[Formula: see text], [Formula: see text]). Reply premiums clustered into three premium bursts from late March to mid-May 2024. Harm reduction references had higher adjusted replies (IRR [Formula: see text], 95% CI [Formula: see text]-[Formula: see text], [Formula: see text]), while co-occurrence of harm reduction references with legal or enforcement misconceptions was associated with a smaller added reply premium (IRR [Formula: see text], 95% CI [Formula: see text]-[Formula: see text], [Formula: see text]).
Public discussion of BC's decriminalization policy revealed persistent confusion, and legal and enforcement confusion intensified around the May 2024 revision. Burst detection on social platforms can identify when and where confusion concentrates, which supports timely public clarification and service signposting. During future amendments, concise messages about permissible locations and remaining police authority may reduce avoidable enforcement contact and misinformation.

title: Accelerated MR Elastography Using Learned Neural Network Representation.
authors: Xi Peng
abstract:
To develop a deep-learning method for achieving fast high-resolution MR elastography from highly undersampled data without the need for high-quality training datasets.
We first reframed the deep neural network representation as a nonlinear extension of the linear subspace model, then used it to represent and reconstruct MRE image repetitions from undersampled k-space data. A multi-level k-space consistency loss was proposed to learn the network weights and mitigate overfitting. To further enhance reconstruction quality, phase-contrast specific magnitude and phase priors were incorporated, namely the similarity of anatomical structures and smoothness of wave-induced harmonic displacement. The network was trained in a self-supervised manner with empirically fixed iterations. Experiments were conducted using one multi-slice spin-echo and two 3D gradient-echo spiral MRE datasets.
Compared to conventional linear subspace-based approaches, the nonlinear network representation method produced superior image reconstruction with suppressed artifacts and noise from a single in-plane spiral arm per MRE repetition, yielding stiffness estimation (e.g., from a 3D GRE sequence at 2 mm resolution within 1 min, R = 10) comparable to that obtained from fully sampled data.
This work demonstrated the feasibility of using deep network representations to model and reconstruct MRE images from highly undersampled data, a nonlinear extension of the subspace-based approach. Future work will include validation on a larger and more diverse cohort of subjects to further assess its robustness and generalizability.

title: Assessing the reliability of AI-generated responses to patient-oriented lung cancer questions: a multi-platform study.
authors: Erhan Özer; Gizem Gedikoğlu Pirim
abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by patients seeking lung cancer-related medical information. Recent studies have increasingly compared multiple LLMs for patient-facing medical information; however, differences in clinically relevant performance dimensions and consistency across repeated responses remain important areas for evaluation.
Seventy-nine lung cancer-related patient questions were queried across three freely accessible LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini) between December 2025 and January 2026. Responses were independently evaluated by two specialist thoracic surgeons for accuracy, completeness, clinical relevance, and readability, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Reproducibility was assessed through five repeated independent queries using a clinical-equivalence framework, and automated readability was assessed using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level. Ordinal outcomes were analyzed using cumulative link mixed models accounting for repeated evaluation of questions, while reproducibility was analyzed using generalized estimating equations.
All platforms demonstrated high accuracy, with no significant overall platform difference (p = 0.150). Completeness differed significantly across platforms (p < 0.001), with higher ratings for ChatGPT than Claude and Gemini and for Claude than Gemini. Clinical relevance showed no overall platform effect (p = 0.568), although a platform-by-domain interaction was observed (p = 0.046). Expert-rated readability differed significantly (p < 0.001), with Gemini receiving higher ratings than ChatGPT and Claude. All platforms produced content requiring approximately 10th-12th grade reading levels. Reproducibility was high overall (88.6-96.2%), with no statistically significant overall platform effect (p = 0.072).
Contemporary LLMs demonstrated high accuracy and clinical relevance, but differed in completeness and readability. Reproducibility was high across platforms, while all models exceeded recommended patient reading levels. Further patient-based validation is needed before routine clinical integration.
Not applicable.

title: Artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and outcome prediction of intracranial aneurysms: a meta-analysis and review.
authors: Shahin Naghizadeh; Seyedpouzhia Shojaei; Fariborz Faeghi; Mohammadreza Aghamohammadi; Mona Gorji
abstract:
Intracranial aneurysms (IAs) affect up to 5% of the general population and pose a significant risk of subarachnoid hemorrhage if undetected or misclassified. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, have shown promise in enhancing aneurysm detection and outcome prediction. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the diagnostic performance of AI in IA detection and reviewed its applications in rupture risk and outcome prediction.
Following PRISMA guidelines, we screened major databases for studies reporting AI-based IA detection and/or outcome prediction. Eligible studies included comparisons of AI versus clinicians or AI-augmented interpretations. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, and interrater agreement (Fleiss' κ) were calculated. Outcome prediction studies were reviewed narratively.
Twenty studies (n = 20) met the inclusion criteria for meta-analysis. Pooled AI sensitivity and specificity were 0.96 and 0.95 respectively. However, substantial heterogeneity across studies was observed. These estimates should therefore be interpreted as exploratory summaries of reported study performance rather than definitive measures of real-world diagnostic accuracy. Subgroup analysis revealed robust AI performance for aneurysms > 3 mm (sensitivity: 0.98), while performance declined for < 3 mm lesions (sensitivity: 0.75). AI assistance improved clinician sensitivity to 0.92 and increased interrater agreement from κ = 0.67 to 0.86. Review of outcome prediction models showed promising AUCs (up to 0.96) for predicting rupture risk, aneurysm growth, and complications like vasospasm.
AI shows promising performance in intracranial aneurysm detection and outcome prediction, particularly when used as a decision-support tool alongside clinicians. While limitations remain-especially in detecting very small aneurysms and generalizability across centers-AI represents a valuable adjunct in neurovascular diagnostics. Future directions include improved training datasets, multicenter validation, and seamless clinical integration to realize the full potential of AI-assisted neuroimaging and risk stratification.
Not applicable.

title: Skull-Base Synthetic CT from Brain MRI: Development, Independent-Center Validation, and Radiologist Evaluation.
authors: Mahbod Issaiy; Shahriar Kolahi; Diana Zarei; Kavous Firouznia; Aysa Karimi; Hossein Ghanaati
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
abstract: We developed and evaluated a deep learning pipeline for skull-base synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generation from routine non-contrast T1-weighted and T2-weighted brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), focusing on clinically relevant bony anatomy for neurosurgical and radiotherapy workflows. We retrospectively collected 184 manually registered T1/T2/CT triplets for training and internal validation (166/18 split) and 43 cases from a second center for independent-center validation. A three-dimensional Swin-UNETR generator was trained with bone-weighted multiscale reconstruction, perceptual, and adversarial losses. Two board-certified radiologists independently scored 16 skull-base structures, artifacts, and diagnostic acceptability on raw sCT in Hounsfield units (HU), without histogram matching; this blinded review was the primary endpoint. Acceptability was 76.7% for Rater 1 and 67.4% for Rater 2 (pooled 72.1%, cluster-robust 95% CI 58.5-82.6%), with mean structure scores from 2.67 to 4.85 out of 5. Raw sCT showed limited absolute HU calibration (global MAE 364 ± 50   HU, bone Dice 0.38 ± 0.09  ), with a compressed dynamic range in which air and soft tissue were overestimated and dense bone underestimated; histogram-matched outputs, reported as a secondary analysis, reached bone Dice 0.88 ± 0.03  and bone MAE 26.31 ± 5.03   HU. Halo artifacts were near-universal, and false-canal artifacts occurred in 21-30% of cases. The method shows promise as a radiation-free adjunct for skull-base visualization, but the present results do not support replacing dedicated CT for diagnostic, dosimetric, or physics-based applications.

title: Performance of Deep Learning Algorithms for Segmentation of Shoulder Anatomy on MRI: A Systematic Review.
authors: María Albertina Loureyro; Keisuke Tsukada; Youichi Yasui; Keisuke Yonezawa; Wataru Miyamoto; José Ignacio Albergo; Germán Luis Farfalli; Luis Alberto Aponte-Tinao; Hirotaka Kawano
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
abstract: To synthesize the performance and methodological characteristics of fully automated deep learning algorithms for shoulder magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation. This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. CENTRAL, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception through July 17, 2026. The protocol specified fully automated deep learning-based pixel-wise segmentation of shoulder MRI, an expert-derived MRI-space reference standard, and quantitative segmentation metrics. Two reviewers independently screened records; unresolved disagreements were adjudicated by a senior reviewer. Overlapping datasets were linked during synthesis. Of 354 identified records, 169 duplicates were removed, 185 records were screened, and 53 full-text reports were assessed. Thirty-five reports were included (31 journal articles and 4 full conference papers; 2018-2026). U-Net-based encoder-decoder architectures predominated, with additional region-based, transformer, adversarial, and autoencoder approaches. Dice similarity coefficients ranged from approximately 0.81-0.99 for osseous targets, 0.71-0.99 for shoulder muscles, and 0.58-0.94 for tendon or tear regions; intersection-over-union values for tear or surgical-planning regions ranged from 0.45-0.83. MRI protocols and validation designs were heterogeneous, and most reports described retrospective single-center investigations. Five reports used independent external test sets; several others included multicenter images. Overlapping cohorts precluded a valid pooled participant count. Deep learning achieved high accuracy for shoulder bones and rotator-cuff muscles in selected datasets, whereas tear-region performance was more variable. Multicenter patient-level validation and standardized annotation and reporting are needed before routine clinical deployment.

title: Practical Solutions to Common TAVI Complications
authors: Herbert Kroon
abstract: Aortic valve stenosis Calcific aortic valve degeneration mainly affects the elderly population. Approximately 15% of elderly patients have some degree of aortic stenosis (AS)1. Untreated severe AS will lead to heart failure, angina and/or syncope and approximately half of patients will expire within 2 years after symptom onset1, 2. Historically, open heart surgery was the only treatment for severe AS. However, advanced age was a dominant argument to defer surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was contrived as a less invasive alternative to surgery and to fulfill this unmet clinical need. After the first-in-human procedure in 2002, TAVI matured into a guideline recommended treatment of symptomatic severe AS in elderly patients across the entire risk spectrum3-7. Peri-procedural embolization Operator experience, improved planning and implantation strategies and multiple device iterations including smaller profile, repositioning ability and outer sealing fabric converted TAVI into a reproducible and relatively safe procedure8. However, the “Big Five” of complications in the modern TAVI era remain 1) access site complications and bleedings, 2) paravalvular leakage (PVL), 3) acute kidney injury (AKI), 4) conduction disturbances including the need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and 5) stroke9. Up to 5% of patients suffer a neurological event after TAVI, mainly within the first 48 hours8, 10, 11. This finding suggests a direct causative role with the transcatheter valve implantation itself. Transcranial Doppler and brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies revealed debris embolization towards the brain and new brain lesions after TAVI in the vast majority of patients12-15. Most of these embolizations remain clinically silent at first sight but may be linked to neurocognitive decline and frank dementia16. Embolic protection devices (EPD) have been developed to deflect or capture embolized debris on its way to the brain and may possibly reduce brain lesions and neurological events including stroke and neurocognitive decline. Part I of this thesis adds perspective to the etiopathology of TAVI related stroke and the mechanism of action of the current spectrum of cerebral embolic protection devices. We also present insights into the microscopic analysis of debris that was captured with filters during TAVI procedures. Vascular access and complications 1 TAVI typically requires large bore femoral artery access. By default, larger arteriotomies are at higher risk for access site complications and bleedings. A completely percutaneous approach relies on vascular access closure devices (VCD) to manage the arteriotomy and provide patent hemostasis. TAVI in low to intermediate risk patients is associated with a major vascular complication rate ranging between 2 and 8%4, 11. The conventional closure technique is based on sutures and most access site complications after TAVI procedures are related to closure device failure17. A collagen plug based closure device was introduced as an alternative to sutures. Part II of this thesis addresses vascular complications and provides information on clinical outcomes with collagen plug-based VCD. TAVI-related conduction disturbances Acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI are frequent and may lead to heart failure (re-) admissions and impaired long-term prognosis18-22. The atrioventricular bundle pierces the membranous septum between the right and non-coronary cusp of the aortic valve and surfaces along the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), which makes it vulnerable to contact pressure by the implanted transcatheter heart valve (THV) during TAVI23, 24. New left bundle branch block (LBBB) and third-degree atrioventricular block (AV3B) requiring PPI occur in up to a third and quarter of patients, respectively18-22. These conduction disturbances may be transient or remain permanent which is clinically relevant in view of in-hospital stay and overall healthcare costs. Unfortunately, there are no uniform definitions to describe conduction dynamics post-TAVI. Inconsistent reporting makes the interpretation of the literature on this topic challenging. Part III of this thesis will elaborate on what is currently known about the incidence of newly acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI and studies specific features on the baseline and postprocedural electrocardiogram (ECG) to predict conduction dynamics. These insights may help determine the need and timing of PPI and adjust hospital discharge policies.

title: Severe rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury associated with probable Legionella pneumophila infection: a case report
authors: Willis Thompson; Andrew John Mallett; Vikas Srivastava; John Di Giusto
abstract: Abstract Background Legionella pneumophila infection is an uncommon but recognised association with severe rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury. We describe an atypical, predominantly extrapulmonary presentation complicated by several plausible causes of rhabdomyolysis and update the literature since the 2020 systematic review. Case presentation A 78-year-old Caucasian male presented with three weeks of progressive lower-limb weakness, anorexia, weight loss, dark urine, oliguria, and a preceding flu-like illness. Examination demonstrated volume depletion and proximal lower-limb weakness with preserved upper-limb strength. Initial investigations revealed severe acute kidney injury, with creatinine 989 µmol/L, estimated glomerular filtration rate 4 mL/min/1.73 m², urea 40.2 mmol/L, and creatine kinase 33,400 U/L. Despite supportive treatment, progressive oliguria, metabolic acidosis, and hyperkalaemia necessitated haemodialysis. Investigations did not support autoimmune, obstructive or haematological causes; medication-related myotoxicity and metal-ion exposure remained possible. Legionella urinary antigen testing was negative. However, serology demonstrated L. pneumophila serogroup 1 IgM and total antibody titres ≥ 1:512. Without respiratory culture, PCR or paired serology, the findings supported probable recent infection rather than microbiologically proven Legionnaires’ disease. Conclusions This case demonstrates the diagnostic complexity of severe rhabdomyolysis-associated acute kidney injury when several plausible causes coexist. Probable recent Legionella infection was considered a potential precipitating factor. A negative urinary antigen result does not exclude Legionella infection when clinical and epidemiological suspicion persists, although single-titre serology should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Mid-term outcomes of right atrial appendage–derived pulmonary valve reconstruction during transannular repair of tetralogy of Fallot
authors: Ahmet Kuddusi İrdem; Onur Doyurgan
abstract: Objectives Transannular patch (TAP) repair remains necessary when pulmonary annular preservation is not feasible during tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair, but the resulting pulmonary regurgitation (PR) may contribute to progressive right ventricular volume loading and late reintervention. We evaluated early and mid-term outcomes of right atrial appendage (RAA)-derived bicuspid pulmonary valve reconstruction compared with monocusp and valve-free TAP reconstruction. Methods We conducted a two-center retrospective comparative cohort study of 49 patients undergoing TOF repair requiring transannular RVOT reconstruction by a single surgeon. Twenty-two patients underwent RAA-derived bicuspid pulmonary valve reconstruction, 14 underwent monocusp TAP reconstruction, and 13 underwent valve-free TAP reconstruction. The three reconstruction strategies were analyzed separately, with an additional RAA-versus-monocusp sensitivity comparison. Because age at repair differed among groups, an additional sensitivity analysis for the principal echocardiographic outcome was restricted to the overlapping age range of the RAA and monocusp groups. Results Median follow-up was 31.5 months (IQR, 28.0–36.0) after RAA reconstruction, 25.5 months (23.0–34.5) after monocusp TAP, and 30.0 months (26.0–36.0) after valve-free TAP ( p = 0.224). At the last available follow-up echocardiographic examination, moderate/severe PR was present in 1 of 22 patients (4.5%) after RAA reconstruction, 13 of 14 (92.9%) after monocusp TAP, and 13 of 13 (100%) after valve-free TAP ( p < 0.001). The association persisted in the direct RAA-versus-monocusp comparison (4.5% vs. 92.9%; risk ratio, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.01–0.33; Fisher's exact p < 0.001) and in the age-restricted sensitivity analysis [1/16 [6.3%] vs. 9/10 [90.0%]; Fisher's exact p < 0.001]. No patient in the RAA or monocusp group underwent pulmonary valve replacement (PVR), whereas three patients in the valve-free TAP group underwent PVR during subsequent clinical follow-up. Conclusions RAA-derived bicuspid pulmonary valve reconstruction was feasible and was associated with a lower prevalence of moderate/severe PR during mid-term follow-up compared with both monocusp and valve-free TAP reconstruction in this retrospective cohort. The association persisted after exclusion of the valve-free TAP group and in an age-restricted sensitivity analysis. These findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies with standardized longitudinal imaging and longer follow-up before conclusions regarding long-term durability, right ventricular remodeling, or PVR risk can be established.

title: Unilateral laminotomy with bilateral decompression versus standard open bilateral decompression in patients with single-level lumbar spinal stenosis without instability: a single-center retrospective cohort study
authors: Martin Hampl; Filip Blažek; Daniel Pohlodek; Matěj Halaj; Lumír Hrabálek
abstract: Background and purpose Degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis is commonly treated surgically. Standard open bilateral decompression (SOBD) is established, whereas unilateral laminotomy with bilateral decompression (ULBD, “over-the-top”) aims to preserve posterior midline structures and contralateral musculature. We compared 3-year outcomes after ULBD and SOBD in patients with single-level stenosis without instability. Patients and methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients operated between 2017 and 2020 for MRI-confirmed single-level lumbar stenosis without radiological instability were included. The primary outcome was the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) assessed preoperatively and at 12, 24, and 36 months. Secondary outcomes were operative time, hospital stay, and complications. Between-group comparisons were exploratory and used the Mann–Whitney U test or Fisher's exact test. Longitudinal ODI analysis was limited by substantial missing baseline ODI data. Results Of 65 operated patients, 63 were included in the functional outcome analysis: 14 underwent ULBD and 49 underwent SOBD. ULBD patients were older than SOBD patients (mean 59.9 vs. 51.2 years; p = 0.011), while BMI did not differ significantly. Preoperative ODI was available for only 3/14 ULBD and 12/49 SOBD patients. ULBD was associated with shorter operative time (median 60 vs. 80 min; p < 0.001) and shorter hospital stay (median 4 vs. 5 days; p = 0.035). ODI was lower after ULBD at 12 months (median 4 vs. 6; p = 0.049), but not at 24 or 36 months. Complication comparisons were limited by low event numbers. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort, ULBD was associated with shorter operative time and hospital stay. Postoperative ODI was lower in the ULBD group at 12 months but not at 24 or 36 months. Because of non-randomized treatment allocation, substantial missing baseline ODI data, and the small ULBD cohort, comparative functional superiority cannot be established.

title: Pacing in adults with complex congenital heart disease: A narrative minireview
authors: Vasileios Papaioannou; Julia Jones; Fahmi Faraz; David Mayhew; Archana Rao; Matthew Kahn; Sarah Moharem Elgamal; Reza Ashrafi
abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a growing health care problem, as more pediatric patients survive to adulthood every year as the number of patients with complex conditions also increases.As more patients survive, there has been an increase in the need for pacemaker procedures.Historically, there has been a focus on epicardial pacing in the most complex groups.In this review, we examine the background epidemiology, existing evidence for pacing, extraction data in three of the most complex CHD groups-transposition of the great arteries with an atrial switch procedure, patients palliated with a Fontan procedure and univentricular hearts.In this expert narrative review, we have used a broad search strategy of PubMed supplemented with evidence where available from non-congenital cohorts.The evidence in these most complex cohorts can be limited to expert centre opinion, small numbers and mixed paediatric/adult data.We discuss below the available data, the limitations and the novel approaches available in centres to deal with the most complex conditions such as conduction system pacing and leadless pacing with promising results albeit in expert centres only.Whilst current applicability to a wider range of institutions is not yet suggested by the paper, this review hopefully illustrates potential options for consideration and research in the future.

title: Invasive Candida viswanathii infections in critically ill neonates: clinical challenges and management insights from a case series
authors: Domenico Umberto De Rose; Chiara Maddaloni; Ludovica Martini; Alessandra Santisi; Venere Cortazzo; Serena Raimondi; Gianluca Vrenna; Francesca Ippolita Calò Carducci; Laura Lancella; Irma Capolupo; Paola Bernaschi; Marta Luisa Ciofi degli Atti; Carlo Federico Perno; Andrea Dotta; Maria Paola Ronchetti; Massimiliano Raponi
abstract: Background Candida species continue to be a major cause of invasive fungal infections in neonatal intensive care units, with a growing awareness of new non-Albicans Candida species that pose diagnostic and therapeutic problems in critically ill neonates. Candida viswanathii is an uncommon pathogen with poor clinical evidence, particularly in neonatal critical care units. Methods From April to August 2025, we conducted a case series of five newborns admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of Bambino Gesù Children's Hospital in Rome, Italy, who had bloodstream infections caused by C. viswanathii . Whole-genome sequencing (WGS), chromogenic agar evaluation, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and traditional culture were all used in microbiological identification. Broth microdilution was used to test for antifungal susceptibility. Retrospective clinical data on risk factors, treatment, and results were collected. Results Six cases of candidemia were reported in five critically unwell newborns, the majority of whom were premature or had severe congenital comorbidities. All of the patients had central venous catheters and had been in intensive care for an extended period of time. Initial identification methods misidentified isolates as Candida tropicalis , however molecular research revealed a clonal cluster of C. viswanathii . The BCID2 panel failed to detect the organism. All isolates had higher fluconazole minimum inhibitory concentrations, but echinocandins and amphotericin B had lower MIC values. Systemic echinocandin therapy was the primary treatment, with liposomal amphotericin B added in severe instances, as well as rigorous source control measures such as catheter removal and antifungal lock therapy. Microbiological clearance was documented in all six candidemia episodes. Three patients were discharged, whereas two died because of their underlying cardiopulmonary disease. Conclusions Invasive C. viswanathii infection represents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge in the NICU. Advanced microbiological techniques, prompt source control, and targeted antifungal therapy are essential for effective management of this emerging pathogen.

title: Saponarin: a shield against coronary heart disease-related myocardial injury via NF-κB pathway inhibition
authors: Linan Yan; 杨引; Junshan Li; Dongyan Yang; Dong Wei; Lianqun Wang
abstract: Objective Coronary heart disease (CHD) is a major cardiovascular disorder characterized by myocardial ischemia and injury. Saponarin is a natural flavonoid glycoside with anti-inflammatory and tissue-protective activities. This study evaluated the protective effect of saponarin against CHD-related myocardial injury and explored the potential involvement of the NF-κB signaling pathway. Methods H9C2 cells were exposed to DOX alone or co-treated with saponarin. Cell viability was assessed using CCK-8, and LDH release was used to assess cell injury. Cell apoptosis was assessed by flow cytometry and cleaved caspase-3 expression using western blotting. Inflammatory responses were evaluated by measuring IL-1 β and IL-6 mRNA expression using RT-qPCR. NF-κB pathway activity was assessed by western blotting and immunofluorescence staining, and rescue experiments were performed using the NF-κB pathway activator RANKL. In addition, a CHD rat model induced by high-fat emulsion combined with pituitrin administration was used to evaluate the in vivo cardioprotective effect of saponarin. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography, myocardial infarct area was evaluated by TTC staining, myocardial histopathological injury was examined by HE staining, myocardial apoptosis was detected by TUNEL staining. Results Saponarin improved DOX-induced H9C2 cell injury, as reflected by increased cell viability and reduced LDH release. Saponarin also reduced apoptosis, cleaved caspase-3 expression, and IL-1 β and IL-6 mRNA expression in DOX-treated H9C2 cells. In CHD rats, saponarin improved cardiac function, reduced myocardial infarct area, alleviated myocardial histopathological injury, and decreased serum CK, CK-MB, LDH, and cTnT levels. In addition, saponarin reduced myocardial apoptosis and inflammatory factor expression in CHD rats. Given the reported regulatory effect of saponarin on NF-κB p65 and the role of NF-κB p65 in myocardial injury, NF-κB signaling was further investigated. Mechanistically, saponarin decreased p-I κ B α /I κ B α and p-NF-κB/NF-κB ratios and reduced NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation. RANKL-mediated NF-κB pathway activation partially attenuated the protective effects of saponarin against DOX-induced H9C2 cell injury. Conclusion Saponarin alleviated CHD-related myocardial injury, ameliorated cardiac dysfunction, and attenuated apoptosis and inflammatory responses. These protective effects may involve suppression of NF-κB signaling.

title: Association and limited incremental discrimination of the systemic coagulation-inflammation index for Gensini-defined coronary anatomical burden
authors: Zhuo Chen; Palida Abulaiti; Palizhati Abudureyimu; Ying Gao; Zhi Xing; Maolin Lv; Hui Li; Jing Shang; Shajidan Abudureyimu
abstract: Background The systemic coagulation-inflammation index (SCI), calculated as platelet count × fibrinogen/white blood cell count, integrates coagulation-related and inflammatory components, but its value for coronary anatomical burden remains uncertain. We evaluated the association of SCI with Gensini-defined coronary anatomical burden and its incremental discrimination beyond conventional clinical variables and comparative performance relative to established inflammatory indices. Methods Eligible angiography records from a single center were retrospectively analyzed. SCI was evaluated in relation to continuous Gensini burden and high Gensini burden defined by the 75th and 80th percentiles, and was compared with NLR, SII, SIRI, PLR, and MLR. Multivariable regression, nonlinear spline analysis, multiplicity-adjusted comparisons, incremental-performance analysis, sensitivity analyses, and exploratory machine-learning models were applied. Results Higher SCI was associated with lower Gensini-defined anatomical burden in the primary multivariable model, although the relationship was not uniformly monotonic across analyses. For high Gensini burden at the 75th percentile, the adjusted OR per 1-SD increase in log-transformed SCI was 0.843 (95% CI 0.727–0.978). Adding SCI to the clinical base model increased AUC only from 0.764 to 0.766 ( Δ AUC 0.0019, 95% CI −0.0010 to 0.0083). Conventional inflammatory markers, particularly NLR, SII, and SIRI, showed larger estimated incremental gains. Machine-learning findings were exploratory and limited by the selected complete-feature sample and lack of external validation. Important limitations included unavailable ACS classification, uncertain timing of blood sampling relative to angiography and treatment, non-random exclusion of records with invalid or missing SCI components, and inability to verify unique-individual linkage. Conclusions SCI was associated with Gensini-defined coronary anatomical burden, but its incremental discriminatory value was limited and does not support routine clinical use. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized clinical characterization and external validation are warranted.

title: Modeling particle transport in biomedical flows using implicit geometry representations
authors: J. Scott Malloy; Sreeparna Majee; Akshita Sahni; Ricardo Roopnarinesingh; Aditya Balu; Adarsh Krishnamurthy; Debanjan Mukherjee
abstract: Computational analysis of physiological and biomedical systems necessitate efficient geometry representations for high fidelity model predictions, including patient or device specificity. Particle-based Lagrangian computational approaches comprise a valuable approach to gain insights from quantitative velocity and pressure data from computational models. Examples include particle dynamics and transport in human vasculature for diseases such as stroke, thrombosis, and embolisms; and modern targeted drug delivery systems in the vascular network and respiratory airways. However, current particle simulation approaches can bear significant computational expense that scales with both number of particles and background fluid mesh resolution. A significant determinant of this computational expense is the contact resolution between particles and anatomically realistic vessel wall. Here, we develop an efficient particle dynamics model that leverages an implicit representation of real anatomical features using a signed distance field to efficiently resolve particle-wall contact. We outline the underlying algorithmic details, followed by a systematic illustration of performance and accuracy using simplified and analytically defined geometries and flow fields. Subsequently, we present a representative simulation of embolic particles along a human vascular segment where we compare our distance field-based approach against classical wall-contact checks based on assessing particle boundary intersection with triangulated surface mesh. Our approach transforms the underlying Lagrangian contact detection operation into an equivalent Eulerian operation, significantly speeding up bulk particle dynamics computations without significantly impacting accuracy or geometric fidelity.

title: Airway Fire During Left Pneumonectomy: A Case Report
authors: Zhang Yang; Tong Meng; Jiandong Gao
abstract: Abstract Background. Intraoperative airway fire is extremely rare yet potentially fatal, and an oxygen-filled tracheal tube is a major risk factor. Fire during pneumonectomy—in which the airway is simultaneously the operative field, the sole ventilatory route, and the conduit for combustion—is uniquely hazardous. We describe such a case and analyze its mechanism, management, and prevention. Case presentation. A 70-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and a long history of smoking underwent thoracoscopic resection of a centrally located left-lower-lobe squamous cell carcinoma. During left pneumonectomy, while the left main bronchus was being divided with monopolar electrosurgery, sudden flame and smoke indicated combustion of the double-lumen tube, which was judged nonventilatable and urgently changed to a single-lumen tube. Before chest closure, bronchoscopy showed red, edematous mucosa with diffuse black carbonized deposits over the carina and both main bronchi; four intraoperative lavage passes were performed, and three further passes were carried out intermittently while the patient remained intubated in the intensive care unit. He was extubated on the first postoperative day, developed transient atrial fibrillation on the second, and was discharged on the seventh. Histopathology confirmed keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (pT4N2M0, stage IIIB). Conclusions. Recognition of the fuel–oxidizer–ignition triad, and preventive measures adopted before and during bronchial division, are essential. Once a fire occurs, immediate cessation of oxygen, rapid re-establishment of a ventilatable airway, aggressive bronchoscopic saline lavage, glucocorticoid pulse therapy, and supportive postoperative care together supported a favorable outcome; at follow-up the patient had completed five cycles of chemotherapy, with intermittent cough and sputum production and hoarseness attributed to unilateral vocal cord paralysis, but remained able to carry out the activities of daily living without clinically significant laryngotracheal stenosis.

title: AORTIC DILATATION AS A CLUE TO BICUSPID AORTIC VALVE FROM DIAGNOSIS TO TIMELY SURGERY A CASE REPORT AND LITERATURE REVIEW
authors: N. Annane² Z. Bennoui*¹
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Background: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) may be associated with progressive aortic enlargement despite preserved valve function. Selecting the appropriate time for prophylactic intervention requires aortic phenotyping and individualized risk assessment. Case presentation: A 56-year-old man without significant medical history or cardiovascular risk factors was evaluated before surgery for lumbar disc herniation with motor-deficit sciatica. He was asymptomatic from a cardiac standpoint; examination revealed no aortic murmur, blood pressure was 120/70 mmHg, and ECG showed sinus rhythm at 75 beats/min without left ventricular hypertrophy. Chest radiography suggested proximal aortic enlargement. Echocardiography revealed type 0 BAV with morphologically altered cusps but neither stenosis nor regurgitation, and an aortic diameter of 42 mm at both the sinuses of Valsalva and sinotubular junction. Cardiac chambers were normal, and laboratory assessment was unremarkable. Discussion: BAV-related aortopathy requires evaluation independently of valve dysfunction. Current US and European guidance generally supports imaging surveillance at 42 mm rather than prophylactic surgery, in the absence of additional high-risk findings. Conclusion: Comprehensive aortic imaging, familial assessment, and lifelong surveillance are central to management of incidentally identified BAV aortopathy.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Adult Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Latest Evidence
authors: Muhammad Ayhan Amir; Zaiba Tallat; Shah Jahan; Cathrine Nixon; Ali Sanan Ahmed; Toki Babajide; Muhammad Arslan Tariq; Shamanpreet Kaur; Zishaan Haider Abbas; Maisha Samiha
abstract: Acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH) is a blood-conservation technique used during cardiac surgery to reduce allogeneic blood transfusion requirements and perioperative blood loss.This systematic review and meta-analysis (SRMA) aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ANH in adults undergoing cardiac surgery.PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and comparative observational studies published between January 2005 and August 2026.Meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager (RevMan) version 5.4 (The Cochrane Collaboration, London, United Kingdom) with random-effects models.Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MDs), whereas dichotomous outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs); both were reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic and Cochran's Q test.Fourteen studies were included.ANH was associated with reduced postoperative chest tube drainage across eight studies (MD, -66.74 mL; 95% CI, -121.45 to -12.02; P = 0.02; I² = 93%).Across seven studies, ANH was associated with a shorter hospital stay (MD, -0.75 days; 95% CI, -1.00 to -0.51; P < 0.00001; I² = 92%).The pooled analysis of perioperative RBC utilization showed a reduction in the number of RBC units transfused across 10 studies (MD, -0.34 units; 95% CI, -0.61 to -0.07; P = 0.01; I² = 85%).ANH was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) (RR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.67-1.06;P = 0.15; I² = 0%).No statistically significant differences were reported for platelet or fresh frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion.Substantial heterogeneity was observed for chest tube drainage, hospital length of stay, and RBC utilization.ANH may reduce postoperative chest tube drainage, hospital length of stay, and perioperative RBC requirements in adults undergoing cardiac surgery.However, substantial heterogeneity across several outcomes and the absence of statistically significant differences in CSA-AKI and other transfusion outcomes warrant cautious interpretation.Further well-designed studies are needed to clarify its benefits across different cardiac surgical populations.

title: Rapidly Progressive Ascending Aortic Aneurysm Associated With Suspected Giant Cell Arteritis: An Urgent Cardiac Surgical Case
authors: Skander HAFI; Jan Remes; Arnaud Henkens; Silvia Solari
abstract: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) may involve the thoracic aorta and cause life-threatening vascular complications.We report an 80-year-old man with polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) who developed palpitations, dizziness, and intermittent dyspnea.Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) angiography showed an ascending aortic aneurysm measuring up to 78 mm, compared with an approximately 40 mm diameter on a non-contrast chest CT one year earlier, along with focal aortic wall ulceration.Urgent ascending aortic replacement was undertaken using a 32 mm Dacron graft.Inflammatory changes rendered dissection of the aneurysmal segment technically challenging.Histopathology demonstrated lymphocytic aortitis involving the intima, media, and adventitia, raising suspicion of GCA-associated aortic disease.Postoperative hemorrhage required re-exploration on day one, and atrial fibrillation was treated medically.The patient was discharged on postoperative day seven.Fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT) at 47 days showed no metabolic evidence of active large-vessel vasculitis.Rheumatologic review at approximately eight months documented clinical remission of PMR under methotrexate and hydrocortisone.This case highlights urgent surgical management of a rapidly enlarging ascending aortic aneurysm and the diagnostic value of histopathological examination of resected aortic tissue.

title: EIT-based non-invasive measurements correlate with pulmonary arterial pressure in patients
authors: Jonathan G. Boudreau; frederick drouin; Mathieu Rivet; Carlos Fallaque; jonathan toma; Jean‐Marc Lina; Andy Adler
abstract: Abstract Objective. To investigate the relationship between cardiac synchronized timing of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) signals and invasively measured mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) in patients with cardiovascular disease. Approach. EIT, ECG and mPAP were recorded in seven patients as part of routine surgery during an apnoea phase, while pressure changes were induced with phenylephrine. Four waveform timings were considered: the maximum, the maxima of the first and second derivatives, and the tangent intersection. Their delays from ECG R waves defined eight markers across the heart and lung regions. Main results. Across 56 patient marker combinations, the mean absolute Spearman coefficient was 0.74. Marker strength and direction varied across patients and landmarks. Each patient had at least one timing marker with an absolute value above 0.79. The lung second derivative timing marker exceeded 0.90 in four patients, more often than any other marker, but showed weaker associations in the remaining three. Significance. These findings represent the first study of EIT timing and mPAP in patients; it suggests that EIT could be a useful non invasive predictor of clinical pulmonary haemodynamics. However, work is required to combine information from timing markers and to relate EIT values to pressure.

title: The Real-World Spectrum of Coronary CT Angiography Findings: Patterns and Vessel Distribution
authors: Emad Ali Al Khoufi
abstract: Objective: To describe the spectrum of documented CCTA findings, the extent of coronary involvement, and the distribution of involved coronary territories in a tertiary-care clinical dataset. Study Design: Retrospective observational cross-sectional study.Place and Duration of Study: This study was conducted at the Tertiary Cardiac Center, Saudi Arabia, from 6th May 2026 to 30th July 2026. Methodology: This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted in 2026 using historical clinical/procedural records from patients attending the cardiac clinic or catheterization service between 1 September and 31 December 2025. The study was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of King Faisal University in May 2026. After excluding records without a usable coronary CCTA entry and four non-coronary vascular CT entries, 172 eligible CCTA-related records remained. To avoid repeated counting, one index record per patient was used, yielding 153 patients for analysis. Results: Among 153 index CCTA records, 113 (73.9%) documented severe stenosis, total occlusion, or explicit three-vessel disease; 29 (19.0%) documented moderate disease, 3 (2.0%) mild disease, and 3 (2.0%) normal coronary arteries. Five records (3.3%) contained other coronary findings that could not be placed in these stenosis categories. A single or isolated named coronary territory was documented in 104 patients (68.0%), while 40 (26.1%) had multi-vessel involvement. LAD territory involvement was most frequent (102, 66.7%), followed by RCA (52, 34.0%) and LCX (35, 22.9%); multiple territories could be present in one patient. Conclusion: The analyzed tertiary-care records showed a predominance of advanced coronary findings and frequent LAD involvement. These results describe a selected clinical population and should not be interpreted as population prevalence. Standardized prospective CCTA reporting would improve future analyses of disease pattern and distribution.

title: Propensity score matched analysis of 5-year outcomes of transcarotid revascularization, transfemoral carotid artery stenting, and carotid endarterectomy
authors: Eunsaem Cho; Aline Hikari Ishida; Zhixin Lun; Pedro J. Furtado Neves; Rafael Demarchi Malgor; Emily A. Malgor
abstract: Abstract Background Prior studies show variable perioperative mortality after transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS), and carotid endarterectomy (CEA), but data beyond the first postoperative year are limited. This study evaluated 5-year mortality and perioperative neurological complication rates after TCAR, TFCAS, and CEA. Methods A retrospective analysis of patients undergoing carotid artery stenting and CEA from 2016 to 2022 was performed using the Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database. Patients were propensity score matched using clinically relevant baseline characteristics. Bivariate analysis, Kaplan–Meier survival, and Cox proportional hazards regression were used to evaluate 1- and 5-year mortality, with subgroup analyses based on symptomatic status and perioperative stroke. Results In 2,394 matched CEA–TCAR pairs, 1-year mortality was comparable (2,027 vs 1,923 at risk, p = 0.41), with no difference at 5 years (513 vs 51, p = 0.21). In 2,862 matched CEA–TFCAS pairs, CEA was associated with lower 1-year mortality (2,406 vs 2,397, p < 0.0001), and this difference persisted at 5 years (598 vs 284, p < 0.0001). In 1,758 matched TCAR–TFCAS pairs, TCAR was associated with lower 1-year mortality (1,401 vs 1,468, p = 0.0055), but this difference was no longer significant at 5 years (39 vs 165, p = 0.11). Perioperative stroke rates were low and similar across all comparisons; however, perioperative stroke was associated with significantly higher mortality at both 1 and 5 years. Higher mortality risk was associated with symptomatic status, age ≥ 70 years, diabetes, coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and end-stage renal disease. Prior percutaneous coronary intervention was associated with lower mortality only in the TCAR–TFCAS comparison. Conclusions CEA and TCAR demonstrated comparable mortality outcomes at 1 and 5 years. In contrast, TFCAS was associated with significantly higher 1-year mortality than both CEA and TCAR, with this difference persisting through 5 years when compared with CEA. Although TCAR showed a 1-year mortality advantage over TFCAS, this difference attenuated over time and was no longer significant at 5 years. These findings support TCAR as a safe and durable alternative to CEA and suggest a less favorable early survival profile with TFCAS.

title: Beyond Structured Vitals: Semantic-Temporal Alignment for Full-Record ICU Risk Forecasting
authors: Zhichong Zheng; Xiaohang Nie; Xueqi Wang; Yuanjin Zhao; Haitao Zhang; Yichao Tang
journal: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
abstract: Forecasting evolving clinical risks relies on intrinsic pathological dependencies rather than mere chronological proximity, yet current methods struggle with coarse binary supervision and physical timestamps. To align predictive modeling with clinical logic, we propose the Medical-semantics Aware Time-ALiBi Transformer (MATA-Former), utilizing event semantics to dynamically parameterize attention weights to prioritize causal validity over time lags. Furthermore, we introduce Plateau-Gaussian Soft Labeling (PSL), reformulating binary classification into continuous multi-horizon regression for full-trajectory risk modeling. Evaluated on SIICU -- a newly constructed dataset featuring over 506k events with rigorous expert-verified, fine-grained annotations -- and the MIMIC-IV dataset, our framework demonstrates superior efficacy and robust generalization in capturing risks from text-intensive, irregular clinical time series.

title: Ultrasound-based assessment of cardiac and hepatic dysfunction: current status and future directions
authors: Yin-Xia Li; Lei Chen; Peng Chen; Yi-Sheng Wang; Rui Shen
abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a systemic syndrome in which venous congestion and impaired perfusion can produce clinically important hepatic dysfunction. The term cardiohepatic syndrome (CHS) describes this bidirectional interaction, but cardiac and hepatic abnormalities are still often evaluated in parallel rather than as a connected hemodynamic process. Ultrasound is uniquely suited to an integrated assessment because it can characterize cardiac structure and function, systemic venous congestion, hepatic hemodynamics, tissue stiffness, and treatment-related change at the bedside. Conventional transthoracic echocardiography remains the foundation of evaluation, while three-dimensional echocardiography and speckle-tracking techniques improve quantification of right ventricular, atrial, and subclinical myocardial dysfunction. Abdominal Doppler ultrasound, venous congestion scoring, and liver elastography add complementary information, although liver stiffness must be interpreted cautiously because congestion, inflammation, cholestasis, and fibrosis can produce overlapping signals. Artificial intelligence may improve acquisition, measurement reproducibility, and multimodal data integration, but external validation and transparent reporting remain essential. This review summarizes contemporary evidence and proposes a practical, sequential pathway that combines echocardiography, venous Doppler findings, liver stiffness, laboratory biomarkers, and dynamic reassessment after decongestion. The central clinical principle is that CHS should be evaluated as a time-varying cardiohepatic phenotype rather than diagnosed from a single cardiac, hepatic, or biochemical measurement. Integrated ultrasound assessment of cardiohepatic syndrome. Heart failure produces a continuum from myocardial dysfunction and elevated filling pressures to systemic venous congestion, hepatic sinusoidal stress, and potentially fibrosis. A combined protocol uses echocardiography to define the cardiac substrate, venous Doppler ultrasound to quantify pressure transmission, and liver elastography plus biomarkers to characterize hepatic injury. Dynamic reassessment after decongestion helps distinguish reversible congestion from persistent structural liver disease and supports risk-adapted management.

title: Challenges and innovations in cardiac AAV gene delivery as a platform for cardiac regeneration
authors: Gabriella Kabboul; Alejandro Izurieta Muñoz; Muath M. Bishawi; Christopher B. Doering; Rebecca D. Levit
abstract: Gene therapies are at the forefront of potential treatments for cardiovascular diseases, but clinical translation remains limited by poor myocardial access and retention, systemic distribution, and immune-mediated toxicities. Heavily underexplored, the route of administration dictates efficacy and safety, ultimately influencing therapeutic outcomes. This review addresses the role of delivery in overcoming these challenges in cardiac adeno-associated viral therapies. Emphasis is placed on biomaterial-based delivery approaches to improve therapeutic outcomes.

title: Physiological markers of low-altitude exercise load for predicting acute mountain sickness: development of an interpretable machine learning model and research web calculator
authors: Fengbo Miao; Yi Yuan; Shuai Wang; Chengli Tao; Yupeng Liu; Qi Mao; Hualin Zhang; Ning Li; Renzheng Chen; Jianfu Sui
abstract: Acute mountain sickness (AMS) poses a significant threat to individuals ascending to high-altitude regions, yet early identification of susceptible populations remains challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model for estimating AMS risk from exercise-induced physiological responses measured at low altitude. A total of 171 healthy participants were included, with 111 participants (51 AMS events) comprising the development cohort and 60 participants (27 AMS events) forming an external validation cohort. Model development was repeated within a nested cross-validation framework, including LASSO feature selection and algorithm selection within the resampling process. The final locked five-feature model included changes in post-exercise pulse oxygen saturation (ΔSpO 2 ) and cardiac output (ΔCO), sex, smoking history, and drinking history, and combined logistic regression, support vector machine, and random forest by equal-weight soft voting. In the development cohort, pooled outer-fold predictions yielded an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI, 0.791–0.929), an AUPRC of 0.842 (95% CI, 0.748–0.932), and a Brier score of 0.148. The calibration intercept was −0.033 (95% CI, −0.504 to 0.527), the calibration slope was 0.931 (95% CI, 0.664–1.351) and the positive net benefit range was 0.078–0.840. In the external validation cohort, the locked model yielded an AUC of 0.834 (95% CI, 0.723–0.929), an AUPRC of 0.867 (95% CI, 0.758–0.946), and a Brier score of 0.152; the calibration intercept was −0.103 (95% CI, −0.834 to 0.531), the calibration slope was 1.013 (95% CI, 0.655–1.666) and a positive net benefit range of 0.200–0.953. Post-hoc SHAP analysis identified ΔSpO 2 and ΔCO as the two most influential predictors. These findings support an association between low-altitude exercise responses and subsequent AMS. However, the prediction model requires further development and validation in substantially larger cohorts before clinical deployment.

title: Mechanosensing channels PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 regulate mitral valve serotonin-mediated homeostasis and pathophysiology
authors: Emily Hall
abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) pathophysiology involves increased serotonin (5-HT) receptor (HTR) expression and signalling, together with reduced 5-HT transporter (SLC6A4) expression in mitral valve interstitial cells (MVIC). The mechanosensitive calcium channels, PIEZO1 and PIEZO2, regulate cellular responses to a variety of mechanical conditions; however, PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 have not been studied in MR. We investigated the hypothesis that PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 mediate, through 5-HT mechanisms, both homeostasis in normal mitral valves (nMV) and in the pathophysiology of MR.
