title: Differential hypoxaemia before aortic cross-clamping during minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: a case report
authors: Kübra Gözaçık Karakoç; Şahin Kapan; Veli Tackin; Nevzat Erdil
abstract: Differential hypoxaemia, also known as Harlequin syndrome or North–South syndrome, occurs during peripheral cardiopulmonary bypass when poorly oxygenated blood ejected by the native heart competes with retrograde oxygenated blood delivered from a femoral arterial cannula, so that the aortic arch vessels and the cerebral circulation may be perfused with deoxygenated blood. It is well described in venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation but is a less familiar complication of minimally invasive cardiac surgery. We report its occurrence before aortic cross-clamping during minimally invasive mitral valve surgery, whilst native ejection was presumed to persist and pulmonary ventilation had been suspended for surgical exposure. A 38-year-old man with rheumatic heart disease and severe mitral regurgitation (left ventricular ejection fraction 60%) underwent minimally invasive mitral valve surgery through a right anterior minithoracotomy with peripheral cardiopulmonary bypass established by femoral cannulation. Invasive arterial pressure was monitored from the right radial artery. Before aortic cross-clamping, whilst native ejection was presumed to persist, the blood visible in the aortic root vent line of the vented antegrade cardioplegia cannula appeared darker and the right-hand oxygen saturation fell to approximately 50%; arterial blood gas analysis showed a partial pressure of oxygen of 226 mmHg in the oxygenator outflow but only 23 mmHg in the right radial artery, confirming differential hypoxaemia. Two-lung ventilation was resumed, and the right-hand oxygen saturation recovered promptly. A 31-mm mechanical prosthesis was implanted and the patent foramen ovale was closed through the same incision. The patient was extubated 4 h postoperatively without clinically apparent neurological deficit and was discharged on postoperative day 5, remaining in New York Heart Association class I at five months. Differential hypoxaemia can complicate minimally invasive mitral valve surgery when antegrade native output persists. Right radial arterial monitoring provides a sentinel indicator of oxygenation in the brachiocephalic territory and allowed early recognition in this patient. Early restoration of pulmonary gas exchange may limit severe upper-body hypoxaemic exposure and potentially reduce neurological risk.

title: Evaluation of Cardiac Manifestations in Acute Haemorrhagic Stroke Patients
authors: S M Abdul Awal; Biswojit Mondal; Prosad Kumer Sarker; Abul Bashar Md Mahbubul Haque
abstract: Introduction: Stroke remains a major cause of death, disability and socioeconomic burden worldwide. Although neurological injury is the primary clinical concern, acute haemorrhagic stroke can also produce important cardiovascular manifestations through autonomic dysfunction, catecholamine excess, pre-existing cardiovascular disease and direct neurocardiac interactions. These abnormalities may include electrocardiographic changes, arrhythmias, myocardial injury, left ventricular dysfunction and structural cardiac abnormalities. Early recognition may therefore assist risk stratification and clinical management. Objective: To evaluate the cardiac manifestations and associated risk factors in acute haemorrhagic stroke patients. Methods: This prospective cross-sectional observational study was conducted in the Departments of Medicine and Neurology, Khulna Medical College Hospital. A total of 50 patients with acute haemorrhagic stroke were included. Electrocardiography and two-dimensional echocardiography were performed within 24 hours of hospital admission. Demographic characteristics, vascular risk factors, ECG abnormalities, echocardiographic abnormalities and in-hospital outcomes were evaluated. Results: The mean age of the participants was 62.05 ± 9.87 years, with male-to-female ratio of 1.77:1. ECG abnormalities were identified in 74.0% of patients and echocardiographic abnormalities in 58.0%. QTc prolongation was the most frequent ECG abnormality (46.0%), followed by ST-segment depression (40.0%), U waves (32.0%), T-wave inversion (32.0%) and electrocardiographic left ventricular hypertrophy (30.0%). Echocardiography showed diastolic dysfunction in 48.0%, left ventricular hypertrophy in 36.0%, mitral regurgitation in 24.0%, aortic valve calcification in 22.0%, regional wall-motion abnormality in 12.0%, left ventricular systolic dysfunction in 10.0%, aortic regurgitation in 8.0% and left ventricular dilatation in 6.0%. Conclusion: Cardiac abnormalities were highly prevalent among patients admitted with acute haemorrhagic stroke. Early ECG assessment and echocardiography may therefore provide clinically useful information for identifying high-risk haemorrhagic-stroke patients. Medicine Today 2026, Vol.38 (2): 232-236

title: Myocardial remodelling during sacubitril/valsartan therapy in patients with chronic heart failure.
authors: DAVID TABUKASHVILI; V. Kapetivadze; Tamar Lazashvili; Zviadi Maglaperidze
abstract: Abstract: The aim of the study was to identify differences between aliskiren and sacubitril/valsartan in their ability to influence cardiac remodelling, metabolic balance, neurohumoral activation, and clinical symptom severity. A comparative assessment of the clinical effectiveness and impact on the structural and functional state of the myocardium was conducted for two therapeutic strategies in patients with chronic heart failure in Georgia over a 12-month follow-up. The results demonstrated fundamentally different trajectories of therapeutic response. In the sacubitril/valsartan group, early clinical improvement was observed by 6 months, including significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (-6.2%, p<0.001), respiratory rate (-4.5%, p<0.001), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (-10.0%, p<0.05), along with improved oxygen saturation (+3.5%, p<0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction increased significantly already at 6 months (from 34.2±4.7% to 37.4±4.0%, p<0.001) and further at 12 months (40.5±3.5%, p<0.001), accompanied by rapid improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, with 9.3% of patients achieving New York Heart Association I by study end. In contrast, the aliskiren group exhibited slower but more pronounced structural reverse remodelling. Significant reductions in left ventricular end-systolic volume (-15.8%, p=0.009), end-diastolic volume (-17.6%, p=0.016), and end-systolic diameter (p=0.002) were observed only at 12 months, along with a modest but significant increase in ejection fraction (p=0.030). Regression of functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation and a significant decrease in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (-19.7%, p<0.05) were more prominent in this group. Both therapies led to significant improvements in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, including reductions in glycated haemoglobin, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and triglycerides (p<0.05 for all), indicating a favourable systemic metabolic effect. Overall, findings suggest that sacubitril/valsartan may be preferable when rapid clinical stabilization is required, whereas aliskiren may represent an effective therapeutic option for patients with advanced structural cardiac remodelling.

title: Upper Partial Sternotomy Combined With Left Anterior Thoracotomy for Acute Type A Aortic Dissection With Severe Pectus Excavatum: A Case Report
authors: Yuta Watanabe; Tohru Ishimine; Natsuki Suzuki; Naoki Taniguchi; Toshiho Tengan
abstract: We report a case of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) complicated by severe pectus excavatum in a 55year-old woman.Preoperative computed tomography demonstrated severe leftward displacement of the heart, suggesting that standard median sternotomy would not provide adequate exposure.Therefore, an upper partial sternotomy combined with left anterior thoracotomy was selected.This approach permitted ascending aortic replacement with adequate surgical exposure.The patient was discharged home, ambulatory, on postoperative day 35.This case suggests the feasibility of this surgical approach for overcoming anatomical constraints in emergency cases involving severe pectus excavatum.

title: Assessment of Myocardial Performance Index and Aortic Elastic Properties in Patients with Ankylosing Spondylitis
authors: Zahraa Ayed Al-Hassani; Ali Jaber Al-Maamori
abstract: Objective: To assess left ventricular myocardial performance and aortic elastic properties in patients with Ankylosing spondylitis Study Design: Cross-sectional studyPlace and Duration of Study: This study was conducted at the Marjan Teaching Hospital's Rheumatology and Echocardiography Units, Babylon, Iraq. from 1st November 2025 to 31st March 2026. Methodology: There were 60 ankylosing spondylitis patients echocardiography was done for each participant. Myocardial performance index-pulse wave and myocardial performance index-tissue Doppler imaging, aortic strain, distensibility, and stiffness index were assessed by echocardiography. Disease activity was evaluated using Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score and C-reactive protein. Results: Mean aortic stiffness index was 5.9±0.87. myocardial performance index-tissue Doppler imaging correlated positively with aortic stiffness and negatively with distensibility, while Myocardial performance indexpulse wave showed no significant correlations. C-reactive protein-positive patients had higher myocardial performance index values (p<0.001). Moderate disease activity was associated with higher myocardial performance index-tissue Doppler imaging (p=0.020) and Myocardial performance index-pulse wave (p=0.012). Aortic stiffness was the strongest independent predictor of myocardial performance index-tissue Doppler imaging (β=0.453, p<0.001), followed by age (β = 0.296, p=0.019). Conclusion: Ankylosing spondylitis is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction and increased aortic stiffness. myocardial performance index-tissue Doppler imaging may provide a sensitive measure of early cardiovascular involvement.

title: Native Aortic Valve Infective Endocarditis Involving the Mitral-Aortic Intervalvular Fibrosa Caused by Lacticaseibacillus paracasei Presenting With a Prolonged Constitutional Syndrome and Non-diagnostic FDG/PET-CT: A Case Report and Literature Review
authors: Arthiom Cambour; Mihaela Malanca Onica; Nawel Rezzoug; Céline Goffinet
abstract: Lacticaseibacillus paracasei is a rare cause of infective endocarditis (IE) and is frequently regarded as a blood culture contaminant, which may delay diagnosis.A 75-year-old man presented with a six-month history of progressive weight loss, drenching night sweats, and chills without fever.Initial investigations revealed an inflammatory syndrome, while FDG/PET-CT showed only nonspecific findings, prompting evaluation for inflammatory, infectious, and hematologic disorders.Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) raised suspicion for IE, and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) demonstrated a 9 mm vegetation on the mitral-aortic intervalvular fibrosa (MAIVF), without aortic leaflet involvement seen on imaging and with mild aortic regurgitation.Four pairs of blood cultures came back positive for Lacticaseibacillus paracasei, confirming persistent bacteremia.No conventional predisposing factors, including immunosuppression, probiotic use, dental disease, or significant gastrointestinal pathology, were identified.Intravenous antimicrobial therapy achieved microbiological clearance; however, repeat transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated persistent vegetation with MAIVF thinning and cavity formation, suspicious for pseudoaneurysm, prompting referral for cardiac surgery at another institution.The postoperative course was favorable, and the patient was discharged 10 days after surgery.This case illustrates that L. paracasei should not automatically be dismissed as a contaminant and that native aortic valve infective endocarditis involving the MAIVF may present without fever, while FDG/PET-CT may be falsely reassuring.Repeated blood cultures and serial echocardiography remain essential for establishing the diagnosis of endocarditis and guiding management.

title: Atrial Distensibility Predicts Short-Term Prognosis in Fetal Single Ventricle-Type Congenital Heart Disease with Atrioventricular Valve Regurgitation
authors: Yohei Akazawa; Kosuke Yonehara; Haruka Obinata; Ryusuke Numata; Yuma Shibuya; Kohta Takei; Kiyohiro Takigiku
abstract: Abstract We aimed to determine whether the assessment of atrial distensibility helps predict perinatal outcomes in fetuses with a prenatal diagnosis of single ventricle-type congenital heart disease (SVCHD) with atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR). We retrospectively identified 77 consecutive cases of fetuses with SVCHD examined between 2011 and 2023. Atrial distensibility and conventional echocardiographic parameters used to assess the severity of fetal heart failure were measured retrospectively. Fetuses with SVCHD were divided into two groups according to AVVR severity: no-mild or ≥moderate. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of composite adverse events (fetal demise, neonatal death of any cause, and early infantile valvuloplasty). The impact of atrial distensibility on prognosis was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Overall, 77 fetuses were diagnosed prenatally with SVCHD; 9 were terminated, and 8 were excluded due to chromosomal abnormalities. Of the 60 fetuses with SVCHD, 48 and 12 had no-mild and ≥moderate AVVR, respectively. Atrial distensibility was significantly lower in fetuses with SVCHD and ≥moderate AVVR than in those with no-mild AVVR (p < 0.001). Among fetuses with SVCHD and ≥moderate AVVR, atrial distensibility was impaired in fetuses with adverse events compared to those without adverse events (p < 0.05). ROC analysis indicated that atrial distensibility exhibited a significant predictive value for composite adverse outcomes in fetal SVCHD with ≥moderate AVVR (area under the curve 0.90; p = 0.02). Quantitative assessment of atrial distensibility may have clinical utility in predicting the perinatal outcomes of fetal SVCHD with significant AVVR.
